Title: A study on an optimal analytical and an accurate algorithmic landing techniques
Abstract: Landing trajectory optimization is a fundamental challenge in aerospace engineering, traditionally approached by optimal control problem formulation. In practice, for Earth landing, the vehicle is subject to strongly non-linear perturbations, such as drag, wind, and gravity. Indirect control methods cannot deal with these problems, leading to large errors, while direct methods require high computation times when perturbations are not continuous. Thus, in this work, we propose a hybrid algorithm to approximate the solution of nonlinear optimization problems, based on the iteration of the indirect control analytical solution of the non-autonomous linear problem. The algorithm's performance has been studied for the problem of landing rockets on the Earth's surface and compared with a standard boundary value problem solver. The results show that the proposed algorithm tolerates strong discontinuous perturbations, with very small landing error and computation time. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Observations and statistical studies of orbit-driven plasma waves in low earth orbit at very low frequencies
Abstract: The number of resident space objects (RSOs), including debris and inactive satellites, is rapidly increasing, posing a growing threat to operational spacecraft. Additionally, many of these RSOs are too small to be reliably tracked by current radars. A novel solution to this problem is to use the disturbances in the plasma environment to track these objects. Over the last decade, theoretical, numerical, laboratory, and observational efforts have studied the generation and propagation of these disturbances. This study investigates these disturbances statistically using 5 months of Very Low Frequency (VLF) Electric (E) field data collected by the Arase satellite. This represents the first large-scale statistical observational study of RSO-generated waves. Specifically, we use E field power between 1 and 20 kHz from the Onboard Frequency Analyzer, which is part of the Plasma Wave Experiment (PWE) onboard the Arase satellite. We analyze this dataset by comparing the power between an “experiment” population of measurements taken where Arase was in a situation where RSO-generated waves would be observed, and a “control” population where Arase was in a situation where no RSO-generated waves would be observed. For robust comparisons, the two populations should have similar distributions of latitude, longitude, altitude, and time. However, rigidly enforcing this matching results in very small sample sizes. We therefore use three different approaches to this balancing. Our strongest results have a p-value of 1.3e-5, indicating that there is a less than 1 in 77,000 chance that the experiment and control populations are drawn from the same parent population. We take this as strong statistical evidence of RSO-generated waves. These encouraging results bolster the feasibility of using these waves as part of a future detection, identification, and tracking system. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: A comprehensive study of geomagnetic and TEC disturbances in relation to M ⩾ 5.0 earthquakes
Abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated the interaction between multiple layers of the Earth and seismic activity, specifically the lithosphere - atmosphere – ionosphere (LAI) coupling, which is the focus of the present study. Anomalies in LAI parameters, such as variations in geomagnetic field and total electron content (TEC) before seismic activity, have been regarded as earthquake precursors by previous researchers. However, earlier studies used only single parameters and had a limited number of case studies. This study aimed to investigate pre-earthquake anomalies using a dual-parameter approach. Geomagnetic field and TEC variations were used to investigate the relationship between the Earth's layers and earthquakes. Utilising global geomagnetic data and TEC data, a comprehensive analysis was conducted on the variations of geomagnetic and TEC data for the 60 days preceding and five (5) days following the occurrences of the 694 earthquakes with magnitudes greater than and equal to 5.0 (M ⩾ 5.0) in the Japan region in 2011. Following the exclusion of days with geomagnetic storms, referred to as disturbed days, this investigation focused solely on undisturbed days. This study explored and compared geomagnetic and ionospheric disturbances during these undisturbed days preceding the earthquakes. Both geomagnetic and TEC precursors were significantly found in moderate and shallow earthquakes. It was revealed that, preceding the studied earthquake events, anomalous behaviours were evident in both geomagnetic and TEC variations, and these behaviours persisted even on undisturbed days. The study also observed that anomalous TEC parameters occurred within the same time frame as the geomagnetic anomalies, and they were found to be detected a month before the earthquakes. The occurrence rate of the geomagnetic precursors was higher of 65 %, than that of the TEC precursors of 11 %. These observations suggest that the preparation process for earthquakes could impact the ground and upper atmosphere, as described by the LAI coupling mechanism. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Mapping of small scale surface water in Denmark – using deep learning, fusing high resolution geo data and Sentinel-1 SAR
Abstract: Accurate assessment of the freshwater budget – and, as a proxy, its extent – is crucial as climate change and human activities intensify. Similarly, mapping flood extent is essential as flood severity increases. Satellite earth observation data such as synthetic aperture radar and optical imagery play a vital role in surface water and flood mapping on global and regional scales. Their high temporal and spatial resolution enables precise and fast surface water mapping. Deep learning approaches combining synthetic aperture radar with digital terrain model information have recently gained increasing popularity. Surface water masks for model training are usually derived from optical multispectral imagery, using spectral indices such as the Normalised Difference Water Index. Mapping surface water on small spatial scales is traditionally difficult. With the 10 meter resolution of Sentinel-1 & 2, small areas lack information, especially considering synthetic aperture radar's intrinsic noise. Denmark publicly provides high spatial resolution geodata, which we want to utilise to improve small-scale surface water mapping performance. We investigate how high temporal resolution Sentinel–1 synthetic aperture radar data can be combined with the high spatial resolution Danish digital terrain model. Additionally, we show how authoritative governmental data on water bodies can be used and combined to form a surface water mask for model training. We show that models trained with our novel approach outperform a model trained with a Sentinel–2 water index derived mask with regards to minimum detectable surface water surface area. We quantify permanent small scale surface water mapping performance on several sites around Randers and for small scale floods on three manually mapped sites of the October 2023 Baltic Sea flood, with one site validated by a drone image. Lastly, we discuss the observed drawbacks of our newly deployed high–resolution national dataset based surface water mask, subsequently calling for a Danish flood dataset. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: ICESat-2 for evaluating space-borne and national digital elevation models across forest and non-forest landscapes in Kastamonu, Türkiye
Abstract: Technological advancements have revolutionized the production of Global digital elevation models (DEMs). Today, there is an ever-increasing availability of global DEMs for scientific applications. The 12 m TanDEM-X, 30 m TanDEM-X Edited, 30 m Copernicus, and 30 m FABDEM global DEMs, along with the 5 m Turkish national DEM were compared in this study. While the global DEMs result from interferometric synthetic aperture radar, the Turkish DEM is produced by stereo-photogrammetry. The assessment was conducted in forested and non-forested settings. The validation was done using the Ice, Cloud and Land Elevation Satellite-2 (ICESat-2) LiDAR. Generally, FABDEM emerged as the most reliable DEM, achieving the best performance in three settings (whole area RMSE: 2.93 m; forest RMSE: 3.98 m; >70 % canopy closure RMSE: 4.31 m). In contrast, the Turkish national DEM outperformed the other DEMs in two settings (non-forest RMSE: 1.54 m; <70 % canopy closure RMSE: 2.83 m). Global DEMs with improved accuracies may soon replace authoritative national DEMs for various applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Satellite observations of global radio frequency noise and strong interference events at 500 km altitude: basic characteristics and geographical distribution
Abstract: This study presents a comprehensive analysis of Radio Frequency (RF) noise and strong interference events (SIEs) across the time, frequency, and time–frequency domains. The data was collected by the SY15 satellite's Wideband ElectroMagnetic Pulse Detector (WEMPD), which orbits at an altitude of 500 km and within a frequency band of 25 to 75 MHz. The RF noise measurements were acquired during September 26–28, 2023, while the SIEs dataset covers the period from September 2022 to February 2024. The research involved segmenting the globe into 72 distinct regions to examine the geographical distribution of RF noise. The analysis revealed significant regional disparities in noise levels, with notably higher averages observed in the Middle East and India. A particularly ‘quieter’ band was identified within the 35 to 58 MHz range, where the global average noise power spectral density(PSD) in log representation falls below −140 dB re 1 V2/(m2·Hz) (abbreviated as dB hereafter), suggesting its potential for preferential use in detection payloads. The SIEs are mainly powerful radar signals and abnormal discharges. The powerful radar signals come from human activities on the ground, and the PSD in log representation is in the range of −120 to −100 dB, corresponding to the frequency bands of 45 to 48 and 51 to 54 MHz. In addition to the interaction between charged particles and spacecraft dielectric, a significant majority—approximately 95 %—of abnormal discharges are likely to come from the interference of powerful radar signals to spacecraft. The research findings serve dual purposes: informing the selection of payload operation thresholds and payload design, while also laying the groundwork for algorithms that recognize and categorize space RF events. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Capability of lunar regolith with hydrogenous materials as shielding material against GCR and SPE on the surface of Moon studied using OLTARIS
Abstract: Apart from Earth, the Moon is the most frequently observed celestial body and the most probable place of habitation beyond our mother planet. One of the significant challenges for habitation is the radiation resulting from the combination of Galactic Cosmic Rays (GCR) and Solar Particle Events (SPEs) experienced on the Moon's surface. Unlike on Earth, there is no protection for a potential habitation zone on the Moon because of its weak magnetic field and extremely thin atmosphere. Incorporating lunar regolith into habitation shielding on the Moon is a promising approach for providing sufficient shielding while reducing the work involved in bringing building materials to the Moon. The interior wall of the regolith-built habitat could be covered in materials rich in hydrogen, which offer complementary radiation protection when being used together with lunar regolith while simultaneously protecting the interior of the housing from the slightly unsafe lunar regolith. In this publication, we compare several hydrogen-rich materials (polystyrene, polypropylene, Kevlar, Mylar, and Lithium hydride) for this application using OLTARIS simulations of effective dose equivalents inside a simulated habitation model. We find that among the hydrogen-rich materials used together with lunar regolith, lithium hydride for GCR and polypropylene for SPE yield the best shielding properties. Additionally, we investigate the thickness of the lunar regolith necessary to provide shielding against GCR. We also examine the differences in GCR shielding depending on the characteristics of the regolith in different regions of the Moon. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Convolutional neural network design and evaluation for real-time multivariate time series fault detection in spacecraft attitude sensors
Abstract: Traditional anomaly detection techniques onboard satellites are based on reliable, yet limited, thresholding mechanisms which are designed to monitor univariate signals and trigger recovery actions according to specific European Cooperation for Space Standardization (ECSS) standards. However, Artificial Intelligence-based Fault Detection, Isolation and Recovery (FDIR) solutions have recently raised with the prospect to overcome the limitations of these standard methods, expanding the range of detectable failures and improving response times. This paper presents a novel approach to detecting stuck values within the Accelerometer and Inertial Measurement Unit of a drone-like spacecraft for the exploration of Small Solar System Bodies (SSSB), leveraging a multi-channel Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to perform multi-target classification and independently detect faults in the sensors. Significant attention has been dedicated to ensuring the compatibility of the algorithm within the onboard FDIR system, representing a step forward to the in-orbit validation of a technology that remains experimental until its robustness is thoroughly proven. An integration methodology is proposed to enable the network to effectively detect anomalies and trigger recovery actions at the system level. The detection performances and the capability of the algorithm in reaction triggering are evaluated employing a set of custom-defined detection and system metrics, showing the outstanding performances of the algorithm in performing its FDIR task. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: A CCD/CMOS telescope digital twin for Space Situational Awareness
Abstract: Space Situational Awareness (SSA) is the process of gaining and maintaining knowledge of space objects and their operational state. Much of the data that powers SSA activities is collected as images taken by optical sensors. Ground-based image acquisition is a dynamic process that is dependent on the object being imaged, as well as time-varying atmospheric and celestial conditions, and the geographic and optical properties of the optics and its sensor. In this work, we develop a digital twin model of image acquisition focusing on high photometric accuracy for optical ground stations using charge-coupled device (CCD) or complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) sensors. This work provides a high-fidelity photometric model for space objects and background stars and an approach to combine these signals into high-quality synthetic images. Simulated images produced with our model are compared and validated against observations from the Purdue Optical Ground Station (POGS) and the Zimmerwald Multiple Applications Instrument telescope (ZimMAIN). The presented model may be applied to design surveys for operational telescopes or to generate synthetic image datasets for training machine learning models for detecting and tracking space objects. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Exploring land surface temperature (LST) and spectral signatures of Baratang and Diglipur mud volcanoes using ASTER VNIR-SWIR-TIR bands in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, India
Abstract: Mud volcanoes (MVs) are sedimentary volcanoes formed by the escape of overpressured fluids from deep, unconsolidated sediment layers. Studying these geological features is crucial for understanding the degassing processes of deeply buried sediments. In the present study, we utilized the Advanced Spaceborne Thermal Emission and Reflection Radiometer (ASTER) remote sensing data to map the MVs in the Andaman & Nicobar (A&N) Islands and also to analyze the composition of emitted gases of these MVs. ASTER TIR (thermal infrared) bands were used to derive Land Surface Temperature (LST) and map the MVs in the Diglipur and Baratang regions of the A&N Islands. VNIR-SWIR (visible and near infrared – short wave infrared) bands were processed to understand the composition of MVs, along with emissivity images derived from the TIR bands to analyze the emitted gases from these MVs. We identified two MVs in Diglipur and five MVs in Baratang using LST analysis and studied their unique geomorphological characteristics. The LST for the Diglipur MVs ranged from 302.40 K to 302.70 K, while for the Baratang MVs, it ranged from 300.45 K to 300.90 K. Reflectance image spectra for both areas revealed prominent absorption features in bands 2 and 6 of ASTER, indicating the presence of ferrous iron and Al/Mg-OH bond vibrations in the SWIR domain. These spectra were compared with mineral spectra (Nontronite, Pyrophyllite, Quartz, Corrensite, Illite, Chlorite) from the USGS spectral library, based on previous geochemical analysis in the region. Further, emissivity spectral analysis (from TIR bands) was conducted to understand the emitted gases from these MVs. It was found that the lowest emissivity in band 10 of ASTER is associated with the spectral signatures of methane. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Analysis of periodic patterns, noise characteristics, and predictive modeling of polar motion and length of day
Abstract: Earth orientation parameters (EOP) are critical for applications in orbit determination, astronomy, space geodesy, and geophysics. Accurate predictions of EOP rely on the identification of both deterministic periodic patterns and noise characteristics. This study addresses these requirements by analyzing the Polar Motion (PM) and Length Of Day (LOD) time series to determine its stochastic model structure, estimated using least squares variance component estimation (LS-VCE). With this model, deterministic periodic patterns were extracted through least squares harmonic estimation (LS-HE) and validated against colored noise components to identify significant signals. Using the IERS 14 C04 data from January 1, 2000, to December 31, 2019, the study identified the noise as power-law with a spectral index of −1.5, suggesting non-stationary fractional Brownian characteristics. LS-HE detected dominant frequencies in PM–notably the Chandler and annual signals–and in LOD, with annual, semiannual, 14-day, and 9-day signals. Building on these findings, short-, mid-, and long-term prediction model were developed for the PM and LOD time series from September 2021 to December 2022. The predictive model combines the LS-HE-extracted signals and the noise model to generate forecasts. These predictions were compared with other models from the Second Earth Orientation Parameter Prediction Comparison Campaign, demonstrating competitive accuracy, particularly for the initial forecast days. The results validate that combining LS-HE with a realistic noise model provides an effective approach for short-term of the PM and LOD forecasting, meeting the accuracy goals of geodetic and geophysical applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Coupled dynamic modeling and analysis for collecting asteroid soil using a flexible brush sampler
Abstract: Soil collection is a critical component of asteroid exploration missions. To assess and analyze the performance of the flexible brush sampler for regolith sampling on asteroids, this paper develops a coupled dynamic model of flexible multibody systems and granular matter. The discrete element method (DEM) is utilized to simulate the asteroid soil, while the flexible brush is represented using the absolute nodal coordinate formulation (ANCF). The proposed model considers various potential contact scenarios and introduces a serial time integration method to couple the flexible multibody system with the particle system. The validity of the coupling model is then confirmed through comparisons with experimental results obtained under vacuum and microgravity conditions. Based on the validated model, this study investigates the effects of brush rotation speed, brush bending stiffness, gravitational acceleration, feeding speed, and brush roughness on sampling results. The results demonstrate that increases in rotation speed, bending stiffness, roughness, and feeding speed lead to a gradual rise in both the mass of collected samples and the average outlet velocity of the samples entering the sampling tube. However, an increase in gravitational acceleration reduces both sampling efficiency and the average velocity of the samples. Furthermore, while enhancing sampling efficiency, higher loads at the brush's connection points increase the risk of damage and displacement of the sampler. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: An intelligent small end-effector for on-orbit maintenance of CSS
Abstract: End-effectors mounted at the terminus of the China Space Station's robotic arm can be utilized for on-orbit maintenance and upgrade tasks of equipment both inside and outside the station. However, some operations of certain components face challenges due to short operational time windows and limited manipulation space. This study focuses on the issue that the dexterous manipulation of the space manipulator is restricted during on-orbit maintenance operations due to the confined internal space of the Solar Array α Rotation Joint (SARJ). A Special End-Effector for D-Type-Aerospace-Bolts (SED) is designed, intended for the screw tasks of D-Type Aerospace Bolts (DAB) under space-constrained conditions. SED can reach the operational position within 25 s in a confined space of 300 mm × 80 mm × 40 mm, satisfying positional tolerance of 4.5 mm and angular tolerance of 1.2°, to complete the screw tasks of DAB. Based on the constraints and their weights related to trajectory length, movement time, and energy consumption, a task planning algorithm is proposed. This algorithm effectively formulates an optimal task execution sequence for the End-Effectors, contributing to the reduction of operational time in autonomous space missions, enhancing operational efficiency, and mitigating risks to astronauts. The operational effectiveness of the SED in the target environment was verified through simulations and ground experiments. Compared with traditional single-parameter optimal operation modes, the proposed task planning method can obtain a comprehensively optimal task scheme, and reduce the operational cost by approximately 8.4 %. This effectively enhances the quality and efficiency of on-orbit manipulation, contributing to the long-term efficient service of the China Space Station. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Petrography of scoriaceous and unmelted micrometeorites from the Maitri Station, Antarctica collection
Abstract: We analysed ten unmelted fine-grained micrometeorites (FgMMs) and ten coarse-grained micrometeorites (CgMMs), along with eight fine-grained scoriaceous micrometeorites (Fg/ScMMs) and sixteen scoriaceous micrometeorites (ScMMs). Particles were recovered using the density separation technique from sediments obtained by melting Antarctic ice. Based on petrological features, unmelted FgMMs strongly resemble the hydrous matrices of carbonaceous CI, CM, CV and CO chondrites, while CgMMs represent chondrule fragments from both carbonaceous and ordinary chondrites. Texturally, the matrices of FgMMs are characterised into C1, C2, and C3 and their elemental composition, along with ScMMs, are similar to individual carbonaceous chondritic groups and hydrated interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) as well as asteroid Ryugu and Bennu. However, matrices of both FgMMs and ScMMs show depletion in Ni and S. The chemical composition of the mineral grains in FgMMs, CgMMs, and ScMMs does not differ from those reported in previous collections, which may be from similar parent bodies and have a strong affinity for chondrules from carbonaceous and ordinary chondrites. This study suggests that the porous matrix nature of FgMMs material precursors generally aligns with the carbonaceous asteroids’ matrix material. In contrast, the coarse-grained particles may represent asteroids with chondrule-bearing carbonaceous and ordinary chondrites. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: MUF predictions from the IRTAM&INGV model and their validation based on ionospheric oblique soundings over China
Abstract: In the contemporary era, there has been a surge in the development of innovative radio communication systems. However, HF communication, a conventional mode with a long history, continues to play a pivotal role and is undergoing rapid advancements across the globe. The maximum usable frequency (MUF) in HF communication is a crucial parameter influenced by the condition of the ionosphere. Accurate predictions of MUF are essential for ensuring the efficacy of communication. This paper assesses the precision of the methodology of employing the IRTAM combining with the INGV model to forecast MUF. The validation is evaluated by comparing the predicted MUF with the maximum observed frequency (MOF) at each time, as determined by experiments conducted at several ionospheric oblique sounding stations constructed throughout China. The MUF predictions from the combination of the IRI and INGV model are also calculated for comparison. Furthermore, the deviations at different times of the day for different links are analyzed. The results demonstrate that the average RMSE is 2.27 MHz and the RRMSE is 16.6 % over the entire experimental links nationwide. In summary, MUF prediction through the IRTAM&INGV model is simple to implement and of a certain applicability in China. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Improving ecological quality assessment in hilly urban agglomerations in Northeast Sichuan, China
Abstract: Existing ecological quality assessment model, such as Remote Sensing-based Ecological Index (RSEI), primarily rely on vegetation, humidity, land surface temperature and dryness indicators. The integration of air quality indicators, such as Particulate Matter (PM2.5), into RSEI remains limited, which also factor that play a crucial role in ecosystem health. This study aims to explore the ecological quality for Northeast Sichuan from 2003 to 2023 using a modified RSEI (MRSEI) by adding Particulate Matter 2.5 (PM 2.5) as well as replaced NDVI with KNDVI using Google Earth Engine. The ecological quality trends are further evaluated using the principal component analysis method, Theil-Sen + Mann-Kendall test, and Geodetector. The results indicate that: (1) MRSEI outperformed RESI in assessing ecological quality of Northeast Sichuan based on the Pearson correlation and image comparison analysis; (2) The MRSEI model demonstrates strong explanatory power, with the average variance explained by the first principal component exceeding 76 %. From 2003 to 2023, Northeast Sichuan experienced significant ecological improvement, with the mean MRSEI increasing by 24.0 % from 0.43 to 0.54. The results reveal a spatial pattern of “superior conditions in the north and stability in the south”; (3) The Theil-Sen-MK analysis indicates that 88.45 % of the region has experienced positive ecological trends, exhibiting an “east-superior-to-west and south-superior-to-north” spatial differentiation pattern, though some ecological degradation persists in the mountainous areas in the western part of Guangyuan; and (4) Geodetector analysis reveals the dominant influence of the thermal environment and air quality on ecological evolution, while also revealing an increasing impact of anthropogenic activities. These findings provide valuable theoretical insights and practical guidance for ecological conservation and sustainable development initiatives in West China. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Analyzing the spatial patterns and changes in urban green spaces of an under rapid urbanization area through landscape metrics
Abstract: The spatial pattern of urban green spaces has undergone significant changes due to the rapid urbanization. In this regard, the present study aims to analyze the spatial distribution pattern and changes of Urban Green Spaces (UGS) over time in Bojnurd, North Khorasan Province. To achieve these goals, green space areas were extracted using Landsat and Google Earth satellite images for the years 2006, 2013, and 2022. In the next step, landscape metrics at the patch and landscape level were calculated using Fragstats software, and their trends of changes were analyzed. The results show increases in landscape metrics like Total Area (TA), Number of Patches (NP), Landscape Shape Index (LSI), and Splitting Index (SPLIT), indicating greater spatial dispersion of urban green spaces over 16 years. The expansion of smaller green patches is also evident, reflected by decreasing LPI and MESH metrics. Assessing the UGS at patch level showed that UGS area metric declined in all zones, with Municipal district 1 decreasing by 0.22 ha and Municipal district 2 by 0.03 ha, reflecting urbanization's impact. The GYRATE index showed slight fluctuations, while it increased under the Urban Area Comprehensive Plan (UACP) scenario, indicating greater fragmentation. Other metrics like PARA, SHAPE, and CONTIG suggest smaller, more fragmented patches due to urban expansion. UGS assessment at landscape level showed that the total area grew by 59.72 ha, but patches increased significantly from 95 to 198, indicating the fragmentation. The mean patch size (AREA) decreased, confirming smaller patches, while the SPLIT rose, indicating more isolation. Green space per capita in Bojnurd grew to 5.266 m2 in District 1 and 5.032 m2 in District 2 by 2022, with projections of 10.377 m2 and 8.936 m2 under the UACP. City-wide, it increased from 4.059 m2 to 5.591 m2, with a projection of 9.812 m2. By using landscape ecology approach, while analyzing the spatial distribution pattern and its relationship with per capita urban green space, it is possible to improve the connectivity of urban green spaces and, as a result, enhance social and ecological functions in urban planning. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Evaluation of CryoSat-2 ocean products through routine monitoring and a 13-year long consistent time series dataset
Abstract: CryoSat-2 (C2) was launched in 2010 and has been retrieving values of sea surface height anomaly (SSHA), significant wave height (SWH) and wind speed (WSP) ever since. Although these oceanographic variables were secondary aims, an operational CryoSat Ocean Processor was implemented in 2014. This study provides details on the routine monitoring process for the various products alongside additional analyses using a 13-year dataset of quality-controlled Baseline C data. Most of this study focussed on Low Resolution Mode (LRM) data with some specific studies of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) mode. No substantial issues with the data were observed but additional studies of SWH and WSP are recommended. Global mean sea level (GMSL) from C2 has a trend of 4.2 ± 0.3 mm/year which agrees, within uncertainties, from other data sources. Regionally the patterns in SSHA trend agree with other sources. SWH from similar analyses found no significant trend but WSP trend was 3.3 ± 0.2 (cm/s)/year. For GMSL and WSP data from descending passes (C2 moving south) have non-significantly higher trends compared to data from ascending passes. Regionally, apart from a few, small areas (primarily around Southeast Asia), trends in C2 WSP are positive and agree with a previous study using multiple altimeters. Biases have been identified including between LRM and SAR using successive differences in SSHA, SWH and WSP. Similarly, seasonally varying biases between ascending passes and descending passes are found, which in turn vary by hemisphere. Comparisons were made between tide gauges based on data from the Permanent Service for Mean Sea Level (PSMSL) and gridded (1°) SSHA from C2. For both LRM and SAR, the significant correlations were positive and similar, albeit slightly lower, to previous studies. Routine reports compare C2 SWH to that from the WaveWatch3 model (WW3) with the latter on average (mean) ∼15 cm higher with a few exceptions. This was confirmed using WW3 and C2 SWH on the same monthly grid where the difference was found to be 10–20 cm, and all correlations were positive (∼0.8–0.9). There are strong differences between C2 SWH and WW3 by hemisphere (bias is greater in Southern Hemisphere) and the variability of correlations is greater in the Northern Hemisphere. The relationship is more complex as there is some evidence that at low SWH WW3 tends to be higher than C2 whereas at higher SWH C2 SWH is higher than WW3. There is a bias between C2 WSP and that from ERA5 that is negative (ERA5 WSP higher than C2 WSP) at higher WSP and a less pronounced positive bias at low WSP. Comparisons of trends in WSP from C2 compared to ERA5 are more complex and patterns in both do not fully match. These results are possibly as a result of altimeters being unable to resolve low WSP (<∼2 m/s). © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Robust adaptive recurrent neural network observer for flexible spacecraft fault-tolerant attitude control
Abstract: For the flexible spacecraft class, this article introduces a robust adaptive recurrent neural network (RNN) based observer-aided active fault-tolerant attitude control framework. The framework employs a model-based observer augmented with the RNN to diagnose spacecraft actuator faults using the online learning capability of RNNs for unknown nonlinear functions approximation to enhance the observer's fault detection and estimation accuracy. The approach adopts a single hidden layer adaptive RNN to optimize the dynamic response, facilitating robust fault estimation even amidst complex challenges such as flexible structural vibrations, inertial parameter uncertainties, and external disturbances. The observer is synthesized by transforming error dynamics into H<inf>∞</inf> filtering problem, aiming to minimize the effect of lumped disturbances and achieve robust performance. The Observer gains are optimized through the set of linear matrix inequality. The adaptation rules for the neural weight matrices are derived using Lyapunov stability analysis of the closed-loop observer while guaranteeing asymptotic stability and convergence. Furthermore, an anti-unwinding composite fault-tolerant attitude control law is formulated using a nonsingular terminal sliding mode surface. This formulation effectively compensates for estimated actuator faults and system uncertainties without reconfiguration, avoiding the transient effects often associated with reconfigurable control. A comprehensive comparative analysis via numerical simulations further substantiates the superiority of the proposed scheme, demonstrating enhanced fault accommodation and improved system stability. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: LS-VCE based relative and absolute stochastic modeling: methods comparison, influential factors evaluation, and positioning validation
Abstract: An appropriate stochastic model is essential for accurate estimation using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) data. In this study, we comprehensively analyze the factors affecting the accuracy of both relative and absolute stochastic models, using least-squares variance component estimation. The analysis incorporates new signals from BDS, B1C, B2a, and other GNSS constellations. The primary objective is to enhance estimation performance using stochastic models and assess the improvement in positioning accuracy achieved through the application of refined models. The results indicate that zero-baseline (ZB) configurations can reliably estimate stochastic models without being affected by atmospheric interference. By contrast, the performance of single-receiver (SR) setups decreases during periods of ionospheric activity and is sensitive to the choice of sliding window size, with optimal results observed using a 3 s window. SR effectively mitigates the multipath effects and more accurately captures the inherent characteristics of GNSS observations. SR exhibits stronger time correlation than ZB, which is likely attributed to the assumption of ionospheric stability within the window. The time correlation for SR may be influenced by the window size. Furthermore, stochastic models are found to be influenced by antenna type, which should be carefully considered. The stochastic models derived using the ZB and SR methods demonstrate comparable performance in positioning experiments; both improve accuracy by approximately 20 % in the north, east, and up components compared to traditional empirical models. Additionally, their variance closely reflects the actual positioning error, underscoring their improved reliability. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Postseismic deformation analysis of the 2018 Lombok, Indonesia, earthquake inferred from GNSS data
Abstract: The postseismic deformation associated with the 2018 Lombok earthquake was investigated using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) data recorded shortly after the earthquake sequence began. The combination of the local velocity model and the AK135 model was applied to define the rheological structure for viscoelastic relaxation modeling. Viscoelastic relaxation was modeled using the Maxwell viscoelastic response of a layered spherical Earth model. The optimum rheological model revealed a 35 km thick elastic layer and an asthenosphere with a Maxwell viscosity of 2.0 × 1017 Pa s. Surface displacement due to viscoelastic relaxation derived from the local velocity model is approximately ten times larger than that obtained using the global velocity model. These results indicate that applying the local velocity model leads to a thinner elastic layer, a more fluid asthenosphere, and more significant deformation compared to other models. In addition to viscoelastic relaxation, afterslip was identified as another physical mechanism contributing to the observed postseismic deformation. The afterslip distribution on the fault interface was modeled using a geodetic inversion method employing Akaike's Bayesian Information Criterion, revealing the maximum slip primarily occurring at shallow depths of the fault. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Topographic assessment and estimation of in-situ construction materials for lunar launch and landing pad construction
Abstract: Establishing long-term infrastructure on the Moon necessitates efficient site selection and material planning, especially in the context of in-situ resource utilization (ISRU). This study presents a topographic assessment and material quantification for the construction of a lunar launch and landing pad (LLP) near the rim of Shackleton Crater at the lunar South Pole. Using high-resolution Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) data, the study integrates surface roughness and slope metrics to evaluate terrain suitability and excavation requirements. Surface Roughness Index (SRI) was assessed through root-mean-square (RMS) height, surface area ratio (SAR), and slope-based metrics, while slope analysis identified flat zones conducive to efficient construction. Six potential 100-meter LLP sites were selected and evaluated through material quantification. Results show that SRI-optimized locations offer terrain consistency with minimal fill needs, while slope-optimized locations combine flatness with low excavation volumes and favorable cut-fill balance. This approach contributes to sustainable lunar construction by identifying terrain profiles that balance engineering feasibility, construction efficiency, and ISRU potential. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Assessment forest and urban green space vulnerability in Lao Cai City post-typhoon Yagi using remote sensing and machine learning
Abstract: Under the influence of climate change, natural calamities such as typhoons and flooding are increasingly impacting forests and urban green spaces (UGS), particularly in mountainous regions. This research evaluates the susceptibility of these ecosystems in Lao Cai City, Vietnam, in the aftermath of Typhoon Yagi, utilizing remote sensing data from 1989 to 2024 alongside machine learning methodologies. The research presented an innovative hybrid ACO-DMOA model that effectively integrates the variable selection capabilities of Ant Colony Optimization with the multi-objective balancing features of Dwarf Mongoose Optimization, resulting in enhanced accuracy (R2 = 0.884). The results indicated significant changes in land use over the past 35 years, with agricultural land decreasing by 2,450 ha from 1989 to 2009, followed by a rise of 1,680 ha from 2009 to 2024, while forested areas have been reduced due to urban development, mining operations, and inadequate environmental regulations. This ACO-DMOA model distinctly recognized non-linear relationships among critical variables, revealing that correlations between forest/UGS density post-typhoon (R2 = 0.435) substantially increase fire susceptibility, a finding not previously documented in mountainous regions. The vulnerability map indicates that regions classified at levels III and above are primarily situated within urban and agricultural zones. These insights advocate for the implementation of effective management strategies for forest resources and UGS to facilitate recovery and endorse sustainable development in Lao Cai City in the face of impending natural disasters. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Precise orbit determination of Spire CubeSats constellation using the raw observation approach
Abstract: CubeSats, a widely used class of nanosatellites, have made significant contributions to both geodetic and non-geodetic applications by offering low-cost, lightweight, and energy-efficient solutions. Spire Global Inc. has deployed over 120 3U CubeSats into various orbits, each equipped with a STRATOS GNSS receiver, a zenith-looking POD antenna, one or two RO antennas, and an attitude determination and control system. These features make Spire's LEMUR CubeSats ideal candidates for precise orbit determination (POD) and geodetic research. This study presents the first application of the raw observation approach for POD of commercial 3U CubeSats, focusing on 10 Spire GNSS-RO CubeSats with diverse orbital characteristics. The POD algorithm includes essential steps, such as the determination of a priori orbits and inertial quaternions for the Spire LEMUR CubeSats. Precise orbits are determined through both kinematic and reduced dynamic orbit solutions for the year 2020. In-flight calibrated antenna center variations (ACVs) are derived from the POD processing, revealing significant deviations from ground-based calibrations. Moreover, the calibrated ACVs vary among Flight Modules (FMs) with similar satellite buses and orbital characteristics, highlighting the necessity for independent in-flight calibration for each FM. To further enhance accuracy, azimuth- and elevation-dependent accuracy maps are generated from observation residuals and incorporated into the POD processing. The agreement between the reduced dynamic and kinematic orbits results in a 3D RMS difference of less than 5 cm. External validation further supports the reliability of the POD solutions. Comparisons with AIUB solutions for FM099 and FM103 in June 2020 show 3D RMS position agreements of 7.76 cm and 8.92 cm, and velocity agreements of 0.08 mm/s and 0.08 mm/s, respectively. Over the entire year, comparisons between the University of Luxembourg reduced dynamic orbits and Spire official L1B solutions achieve a 3D RMS of 22–29 cm in position and 0.25–1.04 mm/s in velocity. These results demonstrate the robustness of the raw observation approach for CubeSat POD and its potential to advance geodetic applications, such as the recovery of Earth's gravity field. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Knowledge distillation based adaptive deformable perceptron for remote sensing image road extraction
Abstract: Automatic extraction of road information using remote sensing technology has been widely applied in various fields, including autonomous driving navigation, cartography updates, land-resource surveys, urban planning, and traffic management. Deep learning algorithms have demonstrated significant potential for automatic road interpretation from remote sensing images. However, road features often exhibit complex global correlations and scale variability in spatial-spectral contexts. Current deep neural networks struggle to effectively model the interdependence of multi-scale shape features and global semantics in complex remote sensing scenes. Additionally, shallow and intermediate features containing road spatial-shape information are often mixed with background features, causing ambiguity and confusion in decoding, which hampers the accurate restoration of road spatial structures. To address these challenges, this study proposed an adaptive deformable perceptron based on a Transformer that leverages a multi-scale local context and global semantics. The encoder employs depth-wise separable convolutions with multi-scale kernels to capture local features from different receptive fields. Simultaneously, deformable offsets are predicted and integrated into the multi-head attention mechanism to adaptively match multi-scale information. Furthermore, a cross-level feature alignment module is introduced in the decoder to refine the encoded features, guided by a knowledge self-distillation strategy. Ablation experiments confirmed that the proposed modules improve predictive accuracy for road detection on two public datasets. Comparative experiments further verified that the model outperforms other state-of-the-art methods. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Ionospheric TEC response at mid and low latitudes to Solar wind oscillations on November 5th, 1997
Abstract: This study analyzes the effect of solar wind on magnetospheric convection and how magnetospheric electric fields can penetrate the ionosphere at mid-latitudes and low latitudes. We investigate ionospheric plasma disturbances at mid-latitudes during a transient event characterized by an interplanetary magnetic field oscillating with a period of 2 h, while solar wind pressure remained stable. The ionospheric response is assessed through vertically integrated total electron content (VTEC) calculated from GNSS observations and electron density in the F layer measured by the Millstone Hill incoherent radar. Additionally, we calculate the vertical movement of the ionosphere using solar data and the geomagnetic field from the IGRF, comparing it with the height variation obtained from the ion velocity of the incoherent radar. Through spectral analysis using Wavelet Transform and Coherence Wavelet, we demonstrate a cause-and-effect relationship between the effects of solar wind on the magnetosphere and its propagation to the ionosphere with ionospheric disturbances. We also show the impact of the penetration of magnetospheric electric fields at stations located at different geomagnetic latitudes, where the oscillatory phenomenon is clearly observed mainly at high and mid-latitudes. Moreover, we analyze stations situated at mid-latitudes with varying geographic longitudes. We find a greater impact of magnetospheric electric fields near the local noon of each station, while stations located on the night side do not demonstrate a response to solar variability. The ionospheric response to solar wind variations shows delays between 0 to 35 min, which can be associated with changes in recombination rates during the day. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Passivity-based adaptive tracking control for spacecraft elliptical orbital proximity operations
Abstract: Passivity-based adaptive tracking control of spacecraft proximity between chief and deputy spacecraft is explored in this paper. Tschauner-Hempel equations are employed to describe the relative motion between two spacecraft, exclusively considering that the chief spacecraft operates in an arbitrary elliptical orbit. The linear periodical time-varying property of Tschauner-Hempel equations is affixed with zero dynamic theory to build an almost strictly passive system, which facilitates a passivity-based adaptive controller to guarantee the closed-loop stability via Lyapunov theory as well as LaSalle's invariance principle. The proposed control scheme is implemented without requiring specific model information of the relative motion dynamics. It hence exhibits robustness to model uncertainties, benefiting from the application of passivity theory. Numerical simulations are illustrated to validate the performance of the proposed adaptive control scheme. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Mission analysis of space-based small camera for space debris detection
Abstract: Current space debris observations and tracking aren't able to detect smaller debris, which poses a significant risk to space activities. This paper analyses the performance of a star tracker for detecting small space debris. This novel approach aims at improving our understanding of these objects. The ESA MASTER (Meteoroid and Space Debris Terrestrial Environment Reference) model is used to study the probability of space debris detection for a specific population of interest. Moreover, the maximum distance a space debris can be detected was analysed based on PROOF (Program for Radar and Optical Observation Forecasting) and using the camera characteristics, specifically by computing the signal-to-noise ratio as a function of debris size and material. This star tracker's maximum distance performance results are then applied together with detectability constraints to simulate, using ESA/ESOC GODOT libraries, when a debris is observed by the camera in space. The results demonstrate that the optical device could detect smaller debris in some of the orbits indicated by MASTER. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Ramp width of quasi-perpendicular supercritical shocks from multi-spacecraft data
Abstract: This study investigates the ramp width of quasi-perpendicular supercritical shocks using high-resolution magnetic field data from the Cluster and Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) spacecraft missions. A statistical analysis of 54 shock crossings examined the relationship between ramp width, ion-scale dynamics, and key shock parameters, including the magnetosonic Mach number (M<inf>ms</inf>) and the shock normal angle (θ<inf>Bn</inf>). The results showed that ramp width, normalized to the ion inertial length (c/ω<inf>i</inf>) or ion gyroradius (v<inf>sh,n</inf>/Ω<inf>ci</inf>), increased with M<inf>ms</inf> and decreased as θ<inf>Bn</inf> approaches 90°. This behavior aligns with the compression and reflection dynamics characteristic of perpendicular shocks. A strong correlation between ramp width and the velocity ratio ([Formula presented]) of reflected ions further highlighted the role of ion reflection and gyromotion in determining ramp spatial scales. These findings support theoretical predictions, such as those by Schwartz et al. (1983), which emphasized the influence of reflected ions on ramp width in ion-scale units. This study improves our understanding of collisionless shock dynamics by highlighting the role of ion-scale processes in shaping the structure of the bow shock transition region. It focuses specifically on Earth's collisionless bow shock and does not address planetary, heliospheric, or astrophysical shocks, which have different thermal and dissipation conditions. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Multi-sensor analysis of low-level cloudiness and its controlling factors over the Indian Ocean
Abstract: In this study, we analysed nearly two decades (2001–2021) of satellite borne multi-sensor low-level cloud fraction (LCF) datasets and reanalysis meteorological parameters over the Indian Ocean, to examine spatial–temporal variations, trends and susceptibility to influencing factors. Results show higher LCF over the Arabian Sea (AS) and Southern Indian Ocean (SIO), while lower levels are observed over the Bay of Bengal (BoB). Zonal variations in low-level cloud reveal a deeper extension (up to 3 km) over southern region compared to a shallower depth (below 2 km) over northern portion. Seasonal pattern exhibits maxima in LCF during the monsoon season (JJAS), while minima during the pre-monsoon (MAM) and post-monsoon (DJF) seasons across the domain. Trend analysis indicates a significant enhancement in LCF over the Northern Indian Ocean (NIO) (up to 0.003/year), except for a decreasing trend for International Satellite Cloud Climatology Project (ISCCP) dataset. Furthermore, cloud-controlling factor analysis reveals a negative response of sea surface temperature (SST) and latent heat flux (LHF) to the regressed LCF records, while the other selected predictors show a positive response. However, the magnitude and statistical significance of the estimated susceptibility coefficients vary depending on the regressed LCF datasets. Overall, our results underscores substantial variability in LCF responses to meteorological drivers, particularly over the BoB. It cautions against broad generalizations due to methodological differences across LCF datasets and emphasizes the need for future research to focus on key influencing factors to improve predictions of basin-scale low-cloud feedbacks. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Latitudinal variation of ionospheric storm effects on March 22–24, 2024 geomagnetic storm over the African Sector
Abstract: This study investigates the latitudinal variation of the ionospheric response to the geomagnetic storm that occurred on March 22–24, 2024, over the African sector. The analysis incorporates ionospheric parameters such as Total Electron Content (TEC), the critical frequency of the F<inf>2</inf> layer (f<inf>0</inf>F<inf>2</inf>), and the peak height of the F<inf>2</inf> layer (h<inf>m</inf>F<inf>2</inf>), derived from GNSS/GPS receivers and ionosonde data, respectively. These were examined alongside magnetometer observations and thermospheric neutral composition oxygen-to-nitrogen ratio [O]/[N<inf>2</inf>] data. Before the onset of the severe storm at 14:00 UT on March 24, weak to minor geomagnetic activity was recorded between March 21 and 23. Using a ±45% threshold for GNSS-vTEC and ±20% for (f<inf>0</inf>F<inf>2</inf>) and (h<inf>m</inf>F<inf>2</inf>), Ionospheric storm effects were identified. Two equatorial Northern Hemisphere stations-CPVG and DJIG-exhibited vTEC enhancements of approximately 60% (on March 23 at 03:45 UT) and 95% (on March 23 at 23:45 UT), respectively. No significant vTEC variations were recorded at any station until the recovery phase of the March 24 storm began around 16:51 UT. Thereafter, positive ionospheric storm effects were detected at stations DYNG and MAL2, each showing vTEC enhancements of around 75% above the threshold. The most pronounced increase was observed at station YKRO, with an 128% enhancement, while the smallest vTEC increase of 50% occurred at station DJIG. Similarly, on March 22–23, 2024, f<inf>0</inf>F<inf>2</inf> increased by 44% at AS00Q, 36% at AT138, and 30% at GR13L, with h<inf>m</inf>F<inf>2</inf> also rising over 30% at AT138 and GR13L. During the March 24 storm recovery phase, f<inf>0</inf>F<inf>2</inf> peaked at 78% at AT138, while AS00Q showed a 44% depletion. These positive ionospheric storm effects are primarily attributed to the combined influence of Prompt Penetration Electric Fields (PPEF) and the enhanced [O]/[N<inf>2</inf>] ratio. In addition, Ionosonde stations recorded negative ionospheric storm in f<inf>o</inf>F<inf>2</inf> and h<inf>m</inf>F<inf>2</inf> during the local daytime of the storm's recovery phase, which can be attributed to westward DDEF. Furthermore, ROTI values during March 22–23 were generally comparable to those observed during geomagnetically quiet conditions. Following the onset of the storm's recovery phase, however, ionospheric irregularities were suppressed across low/equatorial latitude stations. Suppression of ionospheric irregularities was further corroborated by ionograms from the low-latitude ionosonde station AS00Q, which revealed a clear attenuation of ionospheric spread-F after the start of the recovery phase. This indicates the role of westward Disturbance Dynamo Electric Fields (DDEF) in regulating these irregularities. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Spatial disaggregation of coarse-scaled gridded rainfall data using open-source earth observation in a semi-arid region for water resources management
Abstract: Accurate rainfall estimates at high spatial resolution are necessary for sustainable regional development in a semi-arid region, where agricultural and economic activities are largely dependent on the local rainfall. However, the scarcity of rain-gauge data and the inherent limitations of satellite derived high-resolution gridded rainfall datasets in overestimating light rainfall and underestimating heavy rainfall events emphasize the need for spatial downscaling of the coarse-scaled rain-gauge interpolated data that has shown relatively better accuracy in the estimation of heavier and lighter rainfall events in semi-arid regions. In this study, a Multi-scale Geographically Weighted Regression (MGWR) model based on an integrated downscaling and calibration framework was developed to generate a high-resolution (1 × 1 km) gridded rainfall dataset at monthly and annual time scales from the coarse-scaled (∼25 × 25 km) Indian Meteorological Data (IMD) using seven environmental variables (elevation, slope, wind speed, AET, Day-LST, Night-LST, and NDVI) retrieved from different open-source Earth Observation datasets in a semi-arid catchment in India. The MGWR-downscaled rainfall data (with residual correction) was calibrated with the rain-gauge data using the Geographical Ratio Analysis (GRA) and Geographical Difference Analysis (GDA) methods, and compared with the rain-gauge data of 2002, 2012, 2020, and 2002–2021 to evaluate the performance of these gridded-high resolution products in capturing the intra-annual variations under normal, dry, wet and average rainfall years, respectively. The GDA-calibrated monthly downscaled dataset with an r2 of 0.87, RMSE of 34.84 mm, and a bias of 0.12 demonstrated higher resemblance with the gauge data in comparison to the original-IMD gridded rainfall data (r2 = 0.65, 56.96 mm and 0.08) between 2002 and 2021. This was also supported from rainfall periodicity (estimated with Multi-Taper Method) and variability analysis, wherein GDA-calibrated downscaled dataset exhibited the highest likeness to the rain-gauge dataset. Groundwater Potential Zones (GWPZ) estimated from the original-IMD gridded rainfall data (∼25 × 25 km) had overestimated the ‘High’ and ‘Very High’ GWP zones and underestimated the ‘Moderate’ and ‘Low’ potential zones compared to the GDA-calibrated downscaled dataset. This indicates that the GDA-calibrated downscaled high-resolution rainfall data provides a more detailed representation of spatial rainfall variability, leading to improved delineation of the GWPZ. The approach outlined in this study is geographically scalable and can be used to bridge the high-resolution rainfall data gaps in other semi-arid regions for climate adaptation studies by improving estimation of water balance components, runoff, infiltration, and other key hydrological processes. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Impact of high-intensity long-duration continuous auroral electrojet activity (HILDCAAs) on relativistic electrons in Earth's outer radiation belt during van allen probes era
Abstract: This study investigates the impact of High-Intensity Long-Duration Continuous Auroral Electrojet Activity (HILDCAA) on the relativistic electrons in the outer radiation belt of Earth. Utilizing in situ observations from the Van Allen Probe mission of NASA, we conducted a comprehensive analysis to understand the impact of HILDCAA events on the outer radiation belt electron fluxes. A superposed epoch analysis was performed to determine how relativistic electron fluxes respond to HILDCAA events as a function of L-shell, pitch angle, and energy. Results show a significant flux enhancement in the relativistic electron fluxes, predominantly occurring with a delay of 0 to 2 days following the onset of HILDCAA events. The general response indicates that the maximum energy of accelerated electrons reaches up to 6 MeV. Notably, electrons with perpendicular pitch angles exhibit greater enhancement than field-aligned populations, implying a critical role for pitch angle-dependent acceleration mechanisms. While the very-low frequency (VLF) waves, specifically chorus waves, also showed enhanced power during the HILDCAA period, the time-delayed and pitch angle-dependent response related to the onset of HILDCAAs highlights the significant influence of wave-particle interactions, particularly driven by ultra-low frequency (ULF) waves in this context. Rather than classical radial diffusion, typically requiring coherent ULF wave structures, the observed acceleration is likely facilitated by persistent, enhanced ULF wave activity, even in the presence of partial incoherence. This is further supported by ground-based magnetometers and in situ magnetic field observations from the RBSP probe, which demonstrated enhanced power of ULF waves during HILDCAA events. These findings reinforce the pivotal role of ULF waves in particle acceleration processes of the outer radiation belt, with implications for satellite operations and other space-based technologies, both on Earth and in the magnetospheres of other planets. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Land degradation processes in coastal watersheds in northeastern Brazil: a GIS-based assessment
Abstract: Watersheds play a fundamental role in the hydrological cycle, providing essential resources for societal development and supporting human, economic, and social activities. This study aimed to identify the spatial dimension of degradation in watersheds in the northeastern Brazil's coastal region. Cartographic modeling techniques were applied using a Geographic Information System based on a set of variables gathered from various sources. The results showed that extensive agricultural practices, such as grazing and sugarcane cultivation, have negative impacts, contributing to increased soil degradation. The analysis identified more degraded areas in the Rio Capibaribe watershed, which stands out for having a moderately degraded class in transition to degraded. Meanwhile, the Metropolitan Sul and Norte watersheds exhibit lower degradation levels but experience strong urban influence, highlighting distinct environmental pressures in different regions. Additionally, human activities such as livestock farming, agriculture, and urban expansion were identified as the primary drivers of environmental degradation, exacerbating the fragmentation of natural ecosystems. The findings highlight the urgent need for public ecosystem restoration policies that promote sustainable natural resource use, encourage family farming, and integrate practical approaches to address the mapped environmental degradation. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: A novel load predicting scheme for the routing optimization in TDMA-based inter-satellite networks
Abstract: The inter-satellite links in navigation constellations typically adopt a time-division multiple access (TDMA) to balance the needs for ranging and data transmission. However, the TDMA-based inter-satellite network experiences significant transmission waiting delays and high dynamics during data transmission. When the data volume of the navigation service is large, packet loss may occur. In order to solve the multi-objective optimization problem of network transmission delay and packet loss rate, this paper proposes a dynamic network routing adjustment strategy based on load prediction. In this regard, a novel network load prediction method based on a hybrid architecture of long short-term memory (LSTM), dynamic graph convolutional networks (DGCN), and a residual connection (ResConn) is presented. This method further enhances the traditional Floyd routing algorithm based on predicted network load data. The simulation results show that the proposed LSTM + DGCN + ResConn model achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.81 on the test set, which is significantly lower than that of other models. The improved Floyd routing algorithm, based on load prediction, reduces the loss rate of network packets from 0.93% to 0.18%, with only a slight increase in data transmission delay. The percentage of transmission delays less than 30 s exceeds 99%. These results demonstrate that the model can effectively predict the load of TDMA networks, and the enhanced Floyd algorithm employs load prediction data to alleviate network congestion, resulting in a notable decrease in packet loss rates and an enhancement of network reliability, all while maintaining transmission delays within an acceptable threshold. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Examining the altitude dependence of meteor head echo plasma distributions with EISCAT and MAARSY
Abstract: A radar campaign with High Power Large Aperture (HPLA) radars in northern Norway was performed for the Geminids 2022 meteor shower to make measurements of meteor head echoes. The MAARSY (53.5 MHz), EISCAT VHF (224 MHz), and EISCAT UHF (930 MHz) radars were all operated in a zenith pointing direction. The field-of-views for the EISCAT VHF and EISCAT UHF radars were approximately coincident. A novel meteor head echo processing algorithm was implemented for the EISCAT Manda experiment mode, providing details on the meteor head echo range, Doppler shift, and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). The occurrence rate of meteor head echo detections for the three different systems were determined as a function of altitude. To investigate the differences in the meteor head echo detection rates, simultaneously detected meteors from the EISCAT VHF and EISCAT UHF were further examined. An altitude dependence of SNR difference between the EISCAT systems was identified and attributed to changes in the atmospheric mean free path. This data was used to determine a plasma density decay rate as a function of r−χ, where r is the distance from the center of the meteoroid. χ was found to have a value of between 2 to 4 (1/r2 to 1/r4). The meteor head echo detection rate differences between MAARSY, EISCAT VHF, and EISCAT UHF systems can be explained using this plasma density decay rate when the relative radar sensitivities and Rayleigh scattering effects are considered. The results have important implications for the determination of the initial mass of incoming meteoroids and the associated mass-loss rates during ablation. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Space plasma precipitation and repelling processes by field-aligned electrostatic potential in auroral arc and hole in the terrestrial polar regions
Abstract: Electric fields along local magnetic field line are one of effective mechanisms for accelerating space plasmas, as represented by the cases of neutron stars and planetary auroras. In the terrestrial polar regions, anti-earthward electrostatic fields along geomagnetic field lines can accelerate electrons in space plasmas into the Earth's upper atmosphere, generating bright and dynamic auroras characterized by arcs, curtains, curls, etc. One of the acceleration mechanisms producing “inverted V”-shaped features in energy-time/latitude distributions of precipitating auroral electrons, as observed in low-altitude space missions, is due to anti-earthward parallel electrostatic fields. The field-aligned electrostatic potentials, ranging from tens of volts to tens of kilo volts, are a consequence of the dynamo process generated in the dynamically changing magnetosphere. Our satellite instruments observed clear ion flux depletion in the energy range corresponding to localized field-aligned electrostatic potential above the satellite, which was coincidental with the electron precipitation forming the inverted-Vs. With advanced instruments onboard a microsatellite in low-altitude polar orbit, we detected recurring ion precipitation signatures accelerated by earthward parallel electrostatic fields, coinciding with electron flux depletion in the energy range smaller than the electrostatic potential. These precipitating ion signatures were observed in aurora-void regions, which we call “auroral holes” here, a conception newly defined after “coronal hole” of the Sun. These signatures provide persuasive double clues for the earthward electrostatic fields that accelerate ions toward the Earth and prevent electrons from penetrating the upper atmosphere although results in the past satellite missions might show the similar signatures. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: A weighted mean temperature model by integrating FY-4B GIIRS and ERA5 reanalysis data
Abstract: Weighted mean temperature (T<inf>m</inf>) is a significant parameter of high-precision and high-resolution Global Navigation Satellite System Precipitable Water Vapor (GNSS PWV) inversion. We constructed an empirical T<inf>m</inf> model (called the FY-4BTm) by integrating the Fengyun-4B (FY-4B) Geostationary Interferometric Infrared Sounder (GIIRS) and the ERA5 reanalysis data provided by European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). Like other studies, the FY-4BTm empirical model takes into account multiple factors such as the longitude, latitude, and elevation, and at high spatial resolutions of 0.5° × 0.5°. When compared to the 102 radiosonde data in 2022, the annual mean bias and root mean square error (RMSE) of the FY-4BTm model are 0.53 K and 4.92 K, respectively. The FY-4BTm model performs better than the legacy Bevis and GPT3 models with an improvement of 2.09 K and 1.78 K in T<inf>m</inf> respectively, especially in the high-latitude regions of the western and northern parts of the study area (73°E ∼ 140°E, 3°N ∼ 55°N). Compared with the ERA5 reanalysis data in 2022, the FY-4BTm's annual mean bias and RMSE are 0.43 K and 4.16 K, respectively. Its precision is generally the best among the three models, but with a slightly lower stability than that of the Bevis model. With the PWV obtained from GNSS station as the reference, the FY-4BTm model also demonstrates well performance in PWV inversion, with annual mean bias ranging from 0 to 0.2 mm. Therefore, the FY-4BTm model will benefit a lot for GNSS PWV inversion without requiring the users to obtain additional meteorological data. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Simulation and validation of space deployable membrane structures using the absolute nodal coordinate formulation
Abstract: Foldable membrane structures, with light weight and foldability, suit the trend of large-scale, lightweight spacecraft and are used in components like antennas and sunshades. This study models crease dynamics to analyze space deployable membrane structure deployment. A deployment model uses crease elements, including pre - configured ANCF shell elements, constraint and contact models, and a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) parameter - identification method. Experiments and simulations validate the model and analyze the structure. Tensile tests at high and low temperatures identify membrane and crease dynamic parameters. Single - crease deployment experiments and simulations verify the model's configuration accuracy. Simulations show the necessity of the inter - layer contact model. Multi - crease deployment experiments and simulations confirm the model's mechanical property correctness. Comparing high and low temperature simulations reveals low - temperature impacts on deployment. This paper presents an engineering feasible crease modeling method for space membrane structure design and optimization. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Precipitable water vapor retrieved from FY-3G/MWRI-RM observations using machine learning models
Abstract: Water vapor is an essential component of the Earth's atmosphere, and accurate retrieval of precipitable water vapor (PWV) is critical to understanding the Earth's climate and hydrological cycle. In this study, we use the global Fengyun-3G/Micro-Wave Radiation Imager-Rainfall Mission (FY-3G/MWRI-RM) L1 data from October 2023 to August 2024 to construct a high-precision PWV retrieval model. Three machine learning algorithms are used to construct our models: Random Forests (RF), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (Light GBM), and Gradient Boosting Regression (GBR), due to their ability to handle complex relationships between brightness temperature data and PWV retrieval with high precision. Then, the precision of retrieved PWV is evaluated using the fifth generation of European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts Atmospheric Reanalysis (ERA5) PWV and radiosonde PWV. Light GBM demonstrated the highest accuracy with root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 2.151 mm over the ocean compared to ERA5 PWV, outperforming GBR and RF. RF demonstrated the highest accuracy with RMSE of 2.323 mm over land compared to ERA5 PWV, outperforming Light GBM and GBR. In addition, this study compares the FY-3G/MWRI-RM PWV with Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer 2 (AMSR2) TPW and AMSR2 PWL. FY-3G/MWRI-RM retrieved PWV demonstrated higher precision compared to AMSR2 water vapor products when validated against ERA5 PWV. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Multi-satellite mission allocation and scheduling method for large-scale problem
Abstract: The application of multiple agile earth observation satellites (multi-AEOSs) in handling large-scale observation missions has garnered widespread attention. This paper presents the potential game-based allocation method (PGAM) for the large-scale problem of multi-AEOSs constellation. First, the mission planning process is divided into two phases, including mission allocation for the whole constellation and mission scheduling for individual EOSs. A heuristic collaborative mechanism is designed to balance the maximization of observation targets and minimization of waiting time, based on AEOS entry sequence into the area of interest (AoI). The multi-AEOS mission allocation problem is then transformed into a generalized ordinal potential game (GOPG). Consequently, the Nash equilibrium (NE) is rigorously proved to be obtainable. Finally, the local strategy search algorithm (LSSA) is introduced for scheduling individual AEOSs in order to rapidly converging to the NE, in which two strategies combining global and local search are developed. The simulation results demonstrate that the PGAM-LSSA outperforms the competing algorithms in various instances. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Global patterns of equatorial plasma bubbles from ICON data
Abstract: Equatorial plasma bubbles (EPBs) are ionospheric depletions that can disrupt satellite communication and navigation systems. This study examines the longitudinal, seasonal, and geomagnetic variability of EPBs using the full ion density dataset from NASA's Ionospheric Connection Explorer (ICON) mission. A dual-parameter detection method, combining the σ index (σ⩾0.5) and a relative ion density depletion condition (ΔN<inf>i</inf><0), was applied to identify EPBs from 2020 to 2022. The analysis focused on pre-midnight (18:00–23:00 SLT) observations within ±10∘ magnetic latitude, with post-midnight (00:00–05:00 SLT) data included to compare responses under disturbed conditions. Pre-midnight EPBs were especially frequent over South America and the Atlantic sector, where occurrence rates peaked. However, high EPB activity was also observed in other regions, particularly the Indian, Southeast Asian, and East Asian sectors, during equinoxes, consistent with established climatology and the role of solar terminator alignment with the geomagnetic field. EPB occurrence rates were highest in 2022 and lowest in 2020, reflecting increasing solar activity during the ascending phase of Solar Cycle 25. Seasonally, occurrence was highest during the equinoxes, although a December solstice maximum was observed over South America. Under geomagnetically disturbed conditions, pre-midnight EPB rates declined modestly, particularly over South America, though not significantly at the global scale. In contrast, post-midnight EPBs showed a statistically significant increase during disturbed periods. These findings illustrate clear regional and local time dependencies in EPB responses to geomagnetic variability during the early years of the ascending phase of Solar Cycle 25. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Long-term lake water levels in central Chile using satellite altimetry and conceptual hydrological modelling approaches
Abstract: Lakes play a vital role in biodiversity conservation and water regulation but are increasingly affected by climate change and human activity. Despite their importance, long-term water level (WL) records remain scarce for most lakes in the Southern Hemisphere. This study introduces a novel conceptual modeling framework for reconstructing WL dynamics, applied to Lake Lanalhue in south-central Chile over the period 1950–2022. The approach integrates satellite altimetry (Sentinel-3A), validated against in-situ WL data, with global hydroclimatic datasets (ERA5-Land, GLEV, TerraClimate). Validation against altimetric records (2016–2023) shows strong agreement (R2 = 0.71; NRMSE = 0.11 m). Precipitation emerges as the dominant seasonal driver (R2 = 0.86), while evaporation exerting a lagged secondary influence (R2 = 0.67). Climate oscillations modulate variability across distinct temporal scales: ENSO drives high-frequency interannual fluctuations (R = 0.37), while the Antarctic Oscillation (AAO) governs lower-frequency variability (≥5 years; R = 0.60–0.64). A long-term WL decline of ∼5 cm per year is attributed to reduced precipitation and regional warming, amplified by AAO-related circulation changes. The proposed framework offers a scalable, low-cost tool for reconstructing water levels in under-monitored lakes, supporting climate adaptation, environmental management, and long-term hydrological monitoring in remote, data-scarce regions. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
