Title: Design and test of ceramic knife-edge seal for in-situ heating system of extracting volatile matter from lunar soil
Abstract: In the pursuit of accurate lunar soil volatile exploration, in-situ deep space sampling analysis offers unparalleled preservation of sample integrity. A critical challenge lies in ensuring a secure sealing environment. This paper introduces an innovative sealing method utilising a ceramic blade to compress a non-metallic seal. Initially, following a comprehensive multidimensional evaluation of sealing configurations, the ceramic knife-edge compression non-metallic sealing ring solution was determined to be optimal. This approach involves positioning the sealing ring within a grooved cylindrical heating furnace body, where radial compression is achieved through an annular ceramic knife-edge interface, thereby ensuring hermetic integrity. Subsequently, a sealing leakage model grounded in Roth theory was developed to elucidate micro-leakage mechanisms. ANSYS simulation software was utilised to investigate the influence of blade tip radius and temperature, revealing correlations with average stress and contact width, as well as the impact of temperature extremes on sealing efficacy. These findings provided the theoretical underpinning for subsequent ground tests. A dedicated test platform was established, adhering to the industry standard QJ3089A-2018, to evaluate the sealing performance of various seal and blade tip radius combinations under diverse conditions. Results indicated that, under a force of 500 N, PTFE seals compressed by an R0.5 mm blade and PVMQ seals compressed by an R0.6 mm blade achieved leakage rates on the order of 10−8 Pa m3 s−1, aligning with theoretical predictions and demonstrating repeatable sealing capability. This study presents a novel and reliable sealing solution for the precise exploration of lunar soil volatiles, offering a technical breakthrough and robust sealing strategy for future deep space missions. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Analytical calculation of the degree of linear polarization of the OI 6300 Å red line radiation in the auroral region of the Earth's ionosphere excited by protons
Abstract: The degrees of linear polarization of the OI 6300 Å oxygen atom line in the auroral region (near the poles) of the Earth's ionosphere are analytically calculated. Title: Rapid identification of time-varying aerodynamic parameters for aeroassisted vehicle via asynchronous iterative filtering
Abstract: Aeroassisted maneuver represents a promising low-energy and high-efficiency maneuvering mode for orbital operations. Nonetheless, this maneuver necessitates that the vehicle traverse through unstable atmospheric conditions within a short timeframe to achieve orbital energy modulation. Such conditions imply that precise and time-varying aerodynamic parameters are critical to the accuracy of the dynamic model, and consequently, the safety of the flight. This paper proposes a methodology for identifying time-varying aerodynamic parameters through asynchronous iterative filtering. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated under various initial states and aerodynamic parameters, validating both its speed and robustness. Initially, to swiftly and accurately ascertain the initial values of aerodynamic parameters and state quantities in situations where these parameters are unknown and the vehicle state has an initial error, a time-synchronized initial value determination strategy is designed for the flight's beginning phase. Following this, an asynchronous iterative filter is developed by incorporating time delay characteristics from dynamic system theory, enabling rapid and accurate tracking of the time-varying aerodynamic parameters throughout the subsequent flight process. Finally, Monte Carlo simulation analyses are conducted across multiple typical aeroassisted maneuver scenarios. These simulations illustrate the identification effectiveness of the proposed method under various initial states and aerodynamic parameters, thereby confirming its speed and robustness. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: An investigation into the development of equatorial plasma bubbles (EPBs) through satellite traces (STs) using ionosonde observations
Abstract: This study examines the role of Satellite Traces (STs) in ionograms as a precursory signature of Equatorial Plasma Bubbles (EPBs) and Equatorial Spread F (ESF) irregularities. Using digital ionosonde observations from Tirunelveli (8.7°N; 77.8°E; 1.7°N Dip Lat), an equatorial station, we analyzed the occurrence of STs and their association with EPB development during the descending phase of the solar cycle (2014–2020). STs appear as oblique echoes in ionograms, originating from the upwelling walls of Large Scale Wave Structures (LSWS). We examined the role of STs in ESF occurrence, considering solar flux, seasonal, and temporal variations. Our analysis shows that STs frequently occur between 19:00 and 20:00 IST across all solar activity levels and are strongly correlated with post-sunset EPBs. The average time delay between ST appearance and ESF onset is around 30 min, suggesting that STs provide an early indication of EPB development. Additionally, we examined the role of bottomside h'F variations in ESF occurrence across different seasons and solar activity conditions. STs are also linked to post-midnight EPBs, particularly during low solar activity, even when Pre-reversal enhancement (PRE) is weak. These results demonstrate that STs serve as a reliable precursory signature of EPB, improving our ability to anticipate ESF occurrence. The findings enhance our understanding of STs and ESF occurrence during post-sunset and post-midnight hours, contributing to better ionospheric monitoring. *Corresponding author. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Short-term space occupancy and conjunction filter
Abstract: Conjunction analysis (CA) for resident space objects (RSOs) is essential for preventing collisions in an increasingly crowded orbital environment and preserving the operational integrity of satellites. A first and fundamental step in the CA process is to estimate the range of altitudes that each object can occupy throughout an operational screening time of, typically, a few days. In this paper, a method is proposed to analytically evaluate such range of altitudes in a zonal problem model and for a time horizon of generic duration thereby generalizing the concept of space occupancy (SO) introduced in a recent work. The proposed method is exploited to construct a new conjunction filter that considerably improves the classical apogee-perigee filter routinely employed in CA. The effectiveness of the new filter is assessed in a low-Earth orbit (LEO) scenario using a high-fidelity perturbation model across a broad spectrum of orbits and conjunction geometries. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: A random forest-based combinatorial optimization model for altitude-dependent vertical correction of precipitable water vapor in China
Abstract: Accurate precipitable water vapor (PWV) is crucial for studying climate change and weather forecasting. Most existing PWV lapse rate models primarily account for periodic variations, ignoring nonlinear factors, which limits accuracy improvements in PWV correction. To address this, this study proposes a combinatorial optimization random forest PWV correction model (RFPWVC) in China. The model takes into account seasonal and intraday variations by leveraging harmonic functions derived from ERA5 data (2010–2018). In addition, it introduces a random forest algorithm to capture the nonlinear components of PWV lapse rates. The accuracy and applicability of the new model are evaluated using radiosonde PWV data over China from 2019 to 2022, and compared with two existing models: the common PWC correction model (CPWVC), which accounts for periodic temporal variation, and the empirical PWV correction model (EPWVC), which uses a fixed lapse rate of −0.5 mm/km. The results show that the root mean square error (RMSE) of the PWV lapse rate of RFPWVC is 0.12 mm/km with respect to the radiosonde lapse rate, achieving a reduction of 25.7 % and 15.1 % compared with that of CPWVC (0.16 mm/km) and EPWVC (0.14 mm/km), which could significantly improve the accuracy of climate models and weather forecasting in complex terrains. Furthermore, the mean RMSE of PWV for the RFPWVC, CPWVC and EPWVC models are 1.72 mm, 1.96 mm and 2.16 mm, indicating that proposed model outperforms existing approaches. The new model also significantly enhances PWV vertical extrapolation, particularly above 3 km where atmospheric water vapor exhibits greater variability due to altitude-related nonlinearities, and demonstrates a clear advantage in the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau. The RFPWVC reduces the propagation of nonlinear errors of lapse rate when extrapolating PWV at different altitudes in China, and can be used for fusion of PWV data from GNSS, radiosondes, and satellite observations, numerical weather prediction and regional climate research. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Optimized YOLOv8 with multi-level attention for satellite image-based landslide detection
Abstract: Detecting landslide events presents a significant challenge in remote sensing, especially as computer vision technologies continue to advance. Landslide detection from remotely sensed images has traditionally relied on manual or semi-automated processes. However, with the rapid development of computational resources, there has been a shift towards automatic methods leveraging deep learning algorithms. Moreover, attention models, inspired by the human visual system, have emerged substantially providing improved solutions for object detection-related problems especially, landslide mapping. Therefore, this research work introduces an enhanced YOLOv8 (nano (n), small (s), and medium (m)) network incorporating popular attention modules, specifically convolutional block attention module (CBAM), efficient channel attention (ECA), and shuffle attention (SA), for enhancing landslide detection accuracy using satellite images. The original YOLOv8 is improved by adding the attention layer discretely after the C2F module within the neck. The addition of an attention layer enables the model to concentrate on the most informative parts of the feature maps combining the capabilities of both channel and spatial attention mechanisms for detecting subtle landslide features. The experiments are conducted using the publicly available Bijie landslide detection database. Standard evaluation metrics, including precision, recall, F-score, and mean average precision (mAP), are used for quantitative analysis. Among the variants tested, YOLOv8n + ResCBAM demonstrates the most promising performance. This study underscores the model's efficacy in facilitating inventory preparation and precise landslide mapping for disaster recovery and response efforts, thereby supporting early prediction models. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Relativistic electron scattering by high-frequency EMIC waves: Test-particle results using self-consistently generated wave fields
Abstract: Theory and simulations predict that the resonant energy of radiation belt electrons interacting with electromagnetic ion cyclotron (EMIC) waves is typically ≳1 MeV, while experimental results suggest that EMIC waves should also be responsible for sub-MeV electron precipitation. The recent report of narrowband (Δf≲0.1f<inf>cp</inf>), high-frequency (0.9f<inf>cp</inf>≲f<f<inf>cp</inf>) EMIC waves—HFEMIC waves for short—suggests the possibility of sub-MeV electron scattering by these waves owing to their large wave frequency (f<inf>cp</inf> denoting the proton cyclotron frequency). To investigate this more quantitatively, we trace test electrons in the HFEMIC wave fields self-consistently generated from a hybrid simulation, and examine the advective and diffusive behaviors of the resultant interactions. Even though HFEMIC waves primarily occur in low density regions outside the plasmapause, the present results show that the wavenumber is large enough to reduce the resonant energy down to as low as several 100s keV. The resulting pitch angle scattering is primarily diffusive for the typical amplitude of HFEMIC waves, but the nonlinear effects also emerge when interacting with the largest-amplitude waves found in the magnetosphere. While the quasilinear theory correctly predicts the overall level of the pitch angle diffusion coefficient, the bounding energy is sensitively dependent on the dispersion relation used (and thus on the warm plasma effect). We expect that low-altitude measurements of energetic electron precipitation can distinguish its characteristic scattering signature, despite the low occurrence nature of HFEMIC waves. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Deep learning-based modeling and prediction of GNSS time series: A comparative analysis of adaptive optimization algorithms
Abstract: In this research, optimization algorithms with adaptive learning rates on Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) time series data are comparatively investigated. For this purpose, five years of GNSS measurement data obtained from the AGRD station located in the Ağrı province of Türkiye were used and incorrect or missing records were detected for a total of 251 days in the dataset. After the missing data were completed using the linear interpolation method, a total of ten different deep learning methods and four different adaptive optimization algorithms (Adam, Adagrad, RMSprop and AdamW) were used to develop separate prediction models and performance evaluations were performed. When the performance of the best combination, the Adam optimized-GRU model, was evaluated based on Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) values, it was found to be 1.58 mm, 1.36 mm and 3.07 mm for the north, east and up components, respectively. When evaluated according to the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) value, it was found to be 1.20 mm, 1.05 mm, 2.33 mm, respectively. As a result of the comprehensive analyses, it has been revealed that Adam and AdamW algorithms are more effective than the others among the adaptive optimization algorithms examined and the deep learning models optimized with these algorithms exhibit superior prediction performance on GNSS time series data. It is thought that the results obtained from this study will be an important reference on adaptive learning optimization algorithms for future studies in the field of GNSS time series and deep learning and will guide the research on the subject. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Spacecraft maneuver detection based on nonlinear uncertainty propagation along decussated orbital arc
Abstract: This paper presents a method for detecting on-orbit spacecraft maneuvers using nonlinear orbital uncertainty propagation. The combined Gaussian mixture model and unscented transform method are used to propagate the orbital uncertainty associated with state estimation errors. This method accounts for potential non-Gaussian effects of the mapping uncertainty through nonlinear orbital dynamics and is applicable to arbitrary dynamical models. Forward orbital uncertainty propagation is used to determine whether an orbital anomaly exists between two observed states, and backward uncertainty propagation is then used to confirm whether the latter observed state was produced by a maneuver between the two observations. The proposed method can detect whether an orbital anomaly has occurred between two sequential orbital states, and uses data association to identify whether the two observations are of the same space object separated by an orbital maneuver. Numerical results show that the proposed method can successfully solve the problem of orbit association after impulsive maneuvers. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Enhanced PPP based on optimization of GNSS broadcast ionospheric model using robust and adaptive constraint
Abstract: Current uncombined (UC) precise point positioning (PPP) with ionospheric constraints mainly relies on Global Ionosphere Maps (GIM), facing two key issues: (1) irrational weighting of virtual ionospheric observations degrades PPP performance; (2) insufficient real-time capability. This study proposes a new method using the GNSS broadcast ionospheric model with robust adaptive constraints to improve UC PPP, preventing unreasonable weighting of virtual ionospheric observations and enhancing positioning performance. To validate the method, GNSS data from 27 global stations during ionospheric calm/disturbed periods are utilized. The UC PPP is conducted with three ionospheric models: Global Ionosphere Maps (GIM), BeiDou global broadcast ionospheric delay correction model (BDGIM), and GPS Klobuchar model (GKlob). For single-frequency UC PPP, the effects of stepwise relaxation constraints and robust adaptive stepwise relaxation constraints on positioning accuracy and convergence time are analyzed. Results indicate that traditional stepwise relaxation constraints prolong convergence and cause solution failures under active ionospheric conditions, whereas the robust adaptive constraint method alleviates performance degradation from irrational weighting. Global-scale analysis demonstrates significant convergence acceleration: UC-BDGIM reduces average convergence time by 5.84 min, and UC-GKlob by 2.31 min. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Mission analysis for the first-ever Saturn Trojan 2019 UO14
Abstract: In mid-2024, asteroid 2019 UO<inf>14</inf> was identified as the first-ever Saturn Trojan through ground-based archival observations and numerical simulations. Exploring this Trojan object with spacecraft may provide definitive information to elucidate the formation processes of our solar system. However, due to 2019 UO<inf>14</inf>’s significant orbital inclination relative to the ecliptic plane and its long orbital period of over 30 years, opportunities to visit this object may be limited to approximately every 15 years. This paper thoroughly investigates potential mission scenarios to the first Saturn Trojan, 2019 UO<inf>14</inf>, to determine the necessary launch window and spacecraft specifications. Initially, assuming a ballistic flight using chemical engines, a meta-heuristic global trajectory optimization algorithm has been developed that incorporates (powered) gravity-assist maneuvers and deep-space maneuvers. Analysis of all potential flyby sequences becomes possible through parallelized iterative search space pruning and evolutionary algorithms. The result indicates that flyby exploration is feasible with a launch window around 2034 and a ΔV ranging from 92 m/s to 1041 m/s within an 11-year mission duration, while a rendezvous can be achieved with a departure around 2035 and a ΔV of 2–3 km/s. Specifically, the itinerary via Saturn requires a ΔV of 2 km/s and a flight time of 24.6 years, while the route via Jupiter results in a ΔV of 3 km/s and a flight time of 13.4 years. Given that the orbital motion of outer solar system objects is relatively slow, low-thrust propulsion, which gradually accelerates the spacecraft, proves to be effective. Consequently, low-thrust trajectories to 2019 UO<inf>14</inf> were examined. The results demonstrate that a rendezvous can be accomplished with nearly the same departure epoch, time of flight, and ΔV as in the ballistic flight, suggesting that low-thrust propulsion is highly compatible with the rendezvous scenario, as it significantly reduces the propellant mass fraction. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Review on magnetic control technology of spacecraft relative motion
Abstract: Spacecraft relative motion control with inter-craft magnetic force/torque has many advantages, such as no propellant consumption and plume contamination, while providing high-precision, continuous, reversible, synchronous, and non-contacting control capability. This technology has been exploited in many spacecraft operation fields, such as docking and separation, swarm flight, noncontact assembly and reconfiguration, etc. In October 2021, two papers on dexterous magnetic manipulation of conductive non-magnetic object were published in Nature, representing one of the novel developments in magnetic control and highlighting a research hotspot of orbit debris removal with rotating magnets. Aiming to reveal the physical mechanism, enabling technology and corresponding application, from introductions to dynamic modeling and dynamics analysis, magnetic device optimization design, control methods, ground and on-orbit experiments, this paper presents a comprehensive review on magnetic control technology of spacecraft relative motion. In addition, this paper also puts forward two key bottleneck problems of spacecraft relative motion magnetic control that need to be solved in the future: feasible magnetic control of far-distance objects and dexterous magnetic control of non-magnetic objects. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: The coupling effect of attitude motion, structural vibration and relative motion on the stability performance of attitude control of space solar power station
Abstract: Space solar power station obtains solar energy in space, and transmits the energy to the ground for users to use through photoelectric conversion technology and microwave wireless energy transmission. It has three characteristics of super-large structure size, super-large structure flexibility, and a wide range of relative motion between subsystems, which makes the coupling effect between the attitude motion, structural vibration and relative motion of the space solar power station, affecting the stability effect of the attitude control system. By fully considering the characteristics of concentrator as the carrier of energy collection and conversion, the coupling dynamics model of space solar power station is constructed, the coupling terms in the coupling dynamics model is studied, and the key structural and kinematic parameters of the subsystems that affect the coupling degree are extracted. In addition, the state space model considering the coupling effect is derived, an attitude control system is proposed, which effectiveness is verified by simulation. The influence of key parameters on the stability of the system is analyzed in detail. The simulation results show that after the attitude control system is stabilized, the coupling effect makes the attitude deviation angle still change periodically. The main parameters affecting the coupling effect are the relative angular velocity of the subsystem, the rotation radius, the mass of the subsystem and the natural frequency, which have different degrees of influence on the change period and the change amplitude respectively. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: A novel robust unscented Kalman filter for spacecraft attitude estimation
Abstract: The problems of packet dropping and non-Gaussian noise in spacecraft attitude estimation systems due to the influence of complex external environments are challenging topics. To solve this problem, a novel robust unscented Kalman filter (NRUKF) is proposed in this paper. First, an augmented model associated with the packet-dropping variable is constructed by designing the coefficient matrix. Then, a robust filter with a recursive process is designed based on the minimum error entropy criterion with fiducial points (MEE-FP). The prior estimates are given using the propagation equation, and the posterior estimates are given using the fixed-point iteration algorithm. Finally, the experimental results show that the proposed NRUKF has excellent performance when the spacecraft attitude estimation system suffers from packet dropping and non-Gaussian noise. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of refugees and displaced persons during the Russia-Ukraine conflict: a nighttime light remote sensing perspective
Abstract: The Russian-Ukrainian conflict, which commenced on 24 February 2022, has precipitated a significant substantial refugee and displaced person (R&DP) crisis. This study presents a novel methodological framework for analyzing the spatiotemporal dynamics of R&DP at a raster scale based on nighttime light (NTL) images and statistical data via data-driven models. We employed comprehensive trend analysis and spatial statistical methods to examine R&DP distribution patterns and their quantitative relationships with NTL radiance values. Data-driven models were developed to quantify the relations between NTL pixel values and the numbers of R&DP and map R&DP distribution at a 500 m resolution. Spatial statistical methods were adopted to identify the spatiotemporal dynamics of R&DP. This study yielded several key findings. The total daily DN values of NTL images in Ukraine decreased by approximately 81.2 % since the onset of the war and as of April 4, 2023. A significant negative correlation between NTL pixel values and the numbers of R&DP with correlation coefficients of −0.93 and −0.74 was detected. The number of refugees in Kyiv, Kyiv Oblast, Cherkasy Oblast, Volyn Oblast, Kharkiv Oblast, Donetsk Oblast, Luhansk Oblast, and Zaporizhzhia Oblast, as well as the number of displaced persons in Vinnytsia Oblast and Cherkasy Oblast, has shown a continuously increasing trend with the progression of the war. Conversely, refugees in Poltava, Sumy, Kirovohrad, Rivne, Khmelnytskyi, and Chernivtsi Oblasts, as well as displaced persons in Poltava, Volyn, Lviv, Rivne, Khmelnytskyi, Ternopil, Ivano-Frankivsk, Transcarpathian, and Chernivtsi Oblasts, exhibited a decreasing trend. This study provides a reference to evaluate the impact of emergencies and can serve as a basis for decision-making in humanitarian assistance. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Spatial downscaling of SMAP soil moisture product by using deep belief network
Abstract: Soil moisture, pivotal for water, energy, and carbon exchange dynamics between the Earth's surface and the atmosphere, drives hydrological modeling, flood forecasting, and agricultural practices. Traditional localized soil moisture measurement methods have led to adopting remote sensing techniques for broader applications. Yet, their limited spatial resolution necessitates downscaling methods. In this study, a machine learning-based method, the Deep Belief Network (DBN), was used as the primary approach for downscaling the 36-kilometer soil moisture product from the SMAP satellite to a 3-kilometer resolution. Additionally, three methods—Random Forest (RF), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), and Linear Regression (LR)—were employed as secondary methods for modeling and comparison with the primary method. Leveraging diverse parameters such as brightness temperature (T<inf>B</inf>), normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI), precipitation, and Albedo, the model was deployed across the western United States over a month and evaluated against Snow Telemetry (SNOTEL) network ground stations. During the test phase, the DBN method demonstrated the best performance with an accuracy of 96 % among the four methods. It was followed by RF with 93 % and ANN with 82 %, both outperforming the LR method, which had a modeling accuracy of 65 %. Vertical brightness temperature emerged as a crucial parameter, while NDVI displayed lower significance in the DBN model. It was demonstrated that by removing 5 SMPs from the total set, the model can achieve a balance between predictive accuracy and simplicity. DBN effectively reconstructed soil moisture values, aligning spatial patterns with SMAP imagery, although assessment by in-situ soil moisture derived from the SNOTEL network showed different results. A comparison between the evaluation results over the entire study area and each land cover revealed that the performance of the downscaling method is different in various land cover types. In ground measurement stations, the downscaled accuracy ranged from R = 0.46 to R = 0.67 and RMSE = 0.013 to RMSE = 0.074, which is improved significantly in comparison to original SMAP imagery ranging from R = 0.21 to R = 0.43. The error distribution analysis highlighted a lack of systematic error, affirming DBN's effectiveness in downscaling SMAP's soil moisture product. This approach exhibits promise across diverse vegetative covers and adaptable temporal ranges, marking strides toward enhanced soil moisture estimation. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Dynamic effects of micro-vibration isolation of control-moment gyros on spacecraft
Abstract: Control moment gyros (CMGs) are widely used as high-torque actuators for agile spacecraft attitude control; however, they inevitably generate micro-vibrations that can induce undesirable jitter. Because CMG-induced disturbances have high frequencies and determinants, passive isolation techniques are commonly employed in engineering practice. This study investigates the dynamic effects of integrating vibration isolators into a spacecraft attitude control system (ACS), focusing on the interactions between the isolators and the ACS. A simplified single-axis dynamic model is first developed to analyze the influence of isolator stiffness and damping on the overall system stability. The analysis reveals that a sufficiently high frequency ratio between the vibration isolator and ACS inherently contributes to system stability. Subsequently, a fully coupled dynamic model is established using Kane's method, which effectively captures the complex interactions among the spacecraft bus, CMG cluster, isolators, and flexible appendages. The proposed modeling approach can be applied to systems with a large number of degrees of freedom while maintaining computational efficiency. Both attitude-holding and maneuvering scenarios are considered to evaluate rigid-flexible coupling behavior, high-frequency micro-vibrations, and low-frequency flexible vibrations. Simulation results demonstrate that the designed passive isolator significantly suppresses high-frequency disturbances, achieving over 80 % reduction in spacecraft jitter and flexible appendage vibration. However, attitude drift and the excitation of lower-order flexible modes are observed in the low-frequency range, particularly during attitude maneuvers. These findings suggest that passive isolation alone may not be sufficient for missions requiring ultra-stable performance, and active isolation should be considered in such cases. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Deep learning-enhanced Koopman operator linearization with LQR control for satellite attitude regulation
Abstract: In this paper, a satellite attitude linearization and LQR control strategy, based on the Deep Koopman operator, is presented to address the reliance on linearization assumptions found in traditional attitude control methods when complex nonlinear dynamics are encountered. By introducing the powerful nonlinear modeling capability of deep neural networks, the complex characteristics of the satellite attitude dynamics system are accurately described, and a high-dimensional linearized model can be obtained without relying on an accurate mathematical model, which can only be trained using historical data. This method not only overcomes the traditional Koopman algorithm's dependence on known physical models or differential equations but also demonstrates better real-time adaptability and generalization ability. Specifically, the Eulerian method is first applied to discretize the satellite attitude-rotation dynamics equations and construct a nonlinear discrete state-space model. Then, the state upscaling is realized based on a deep autoencoder, and the high-dimensional linear dynamic system parameters are designed to capture the behavioral characteristics of the nonlinear system. To restore the physical significance of the high-dimensional state vectors, a decoder is further developed for dimensionality reduction processing, which recovers the low-dimensional state vectors. In addition, we define a comprehensive loss function including autoencoder loss, prediction loss, metric loss, and controllability loss to optimize the learning process of the whole framework. Experimental results show that the proposed LQR controller based on the Deep Koopman operator outperforms other nonlinear control methods (e.g., NMPC and iLQR) in terms of control accuracy and energy loss. Especially for the presence of Gaussian random disturbances, the controller is still able to maintain small tracking errors and low energy consumption, proving its robustness and adaptability. Therefore, this study provides a new theoretical foundation and technical framework for future satellite attitude control, especially in missions requiring fast response and high accuracy, showing significant advantages. Lastly, simulations and comparisons are given to demonstrate the effectiveness and excellent tracking performance of the proposed control scheme. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Multi-objective optimization and cost-benefit analysis of configuration maintenance for the TianQin mission
Abstract: TianQin, a space-based gravitational wave (GW) detector in geocentric orbit, maintains continuous laser links during science operations but requires biannual interruptions when the constellation enters Sun-pointing mode to protect optical payloads from direct sunlight exposure. These planned operational pauses are strategically repurposed for configuration maintenance to optimize subsequent observation cycles. This paper analyzes the trade-offs between the geometric stability and fuel consumption during active orbital control of the TianQin constellation. A segmented cooperative control strategy, based on virtual formation and virtual structure methods, is proposed to simplify the multi-objective optimization problem. The computational efficiency is further improved by fast estimating the optimization indices and by simplifying the dynamics. Due to the segmented reference orbits, this optimization method is applicable to general scenarios where the configuration naturally diverges. By analyzing both the diverging nominal and stable optimized configurations of TianQin, we quantitatively evaluate the benefits and costs of active configuration maintenance, revealing a non-uniformly conflicting relationship between the geometric stability and fuel consumption. The achievable geometric stability is determined in high-fidelity dynamics using local optimization. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: A new tropospheric delay combination prediction model based on time series decomposition and deep learning
Abstract: Zenith tropospheric delay (ZTD) prediction is crucial for high-precision navigation. However, accurately modeling ZTD remains challenging due to its combination of linear and nonlinear characteristics. In this paper, we propose a hybrid ZTD prediction model that separately addresses the trend and seasonal variations. The model decomposes ZTD time series using seasonal-trend decomposition based on loess (STL), and then predicts nonlinear components with a long short-term memory network (LSTM) and linear components with an autoregressive integrated moving average model (ARIMA). The individual predictions are recombined to produce a final forecast, which we call the STL-LSTM-ARIMA model. To assess its effectiveness, we compare it to LSTM, ARIMA, and extreme learning machine (ELM) model. Our results show that the STL-LSTM-ARIMA model consistently outperforms these models across all evaluation metrics, including a root mean square error (RMSE, 1.32 cm), an average normalized root mean square error (NRMSE, 0.56 %), a mean absolute error (MAE, 0.98 cm) and a coefficient of determination (R2, 0.83). Further analysis reveals that the model maintains robust predictive performance across different months, with the highest accuracy observesd in January and lower performance in July. The model sustains exceptional forecasting accuracy for lead times of up to 12 hours, maintaining RMSE < 1.60 cm, NRMSE < 0.7 %, MAE < 1.25 cm, and R2 ≥ 0.75. These results conclusively validate the STL-LSTM-ARIMA model's superior capability and reliability for short-term ZTD prediction. We apply the tropospheric delay parameters predicted by the SLA model to the static precise point positioning (PPP), and the results show that the SLA model-assisted PPP scheme (PPP-SLA) improves the positioning convergence time and accuracy to a certain extent compared to the parameter estimation scheme (PPP-EST) and the parameter estimation scheme for estimating the horizontal gradient (PPP-ESTG). Especially in the U direction, the positioning convergence time is increased by 48.6 % and 47.0 %, and the positioning accuracy is increased by 12.0 % and 7.3 %, respectively. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Multiple solutions of initial orbit determination in cislunar space
Abstract: This research investigates the initial orbit determination (IOD) for objects moving in the cislunar space, using optical observations from both ground- and space-based stations. The proposed method, referred to as the perturbed-Laplace (PL) method, is derived in an approach the same as the conventional Laplace's method, i.e., the IOD problem is transformed into solving a polynomial equation of the pseudo range. The difference is that the polynomial equation is more complex. This study investigates the number of solutions of the polynomial equation. Moreover, key issues associated with the PL method are studied, including the choice of the fitting polynomial to get the first and second derivatives of the optical data, and the influence of the observation errors on the IOD results. For the orbit types studied in this work, we recommend to use a fitting polynomial of order 8 for arc lengths greater than 4 h, and a lower order for shorter arc lengths. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Effects of BDS-2 flex power in daily ionospheric TEC estimation
Abstract: Beidou Navigation Satellites System (BDS) flex power is a function to prevent signal jamming. In this paper, we analyzed the impacts of BDS-2 flex power in daily ionospheric total electron content (TEC) estimation in two regions: an Australia region flex power covered (AUS Region) and an America region flex power not covered (USA Region). TEC estimation involving GALILEO and GLONASS provides the reference TEC values. When flex power of satellites involved was activated all day, there are no significant impacts of flex power on daily TEC estimation in either region. When flex power was activated for only part of a day, daily TEC estimation considering flex power in the AUS Region declines the root mean square (RMS) of TEC estimation by 52.09 %, reduces the TEC bias by 3.26 TECU on average, improves ionospheric-constrained (IC) single-frequency (SF) precise point positioning (PPP) accuracy by 23.04 %, 2.63 % and 3.20 % on average in East (E), North (N), and Up (U) directions, and achieves 4.95 % faster convergence. However, in the USA region, there are no significant differences in daily TEC estimation whether considering flex power or not, attributable to insufficient observations of satellites with flex power. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Automatic localization and characterization of mid-latitude ionospheric plasma structures from all-sky airglow images using deep learning framework
Abstract: This paper brings forth a new automatic approach to determine the propagation parameters (horizontal velocity, propagation direction, and orientation) of mid-latitude ionospheric plasma structures (MIPS) using airglow images recorded by an all-sky airglow imager located at Hanle, Ladakh, India. The proposed approach is an amalgamation of two frameworks – a hybrid deep learning image segmentation model for localization along with automatic determination of parameters using the intensity minima of the MIPS. Designed in the form of a pipeline, the frameworks are executed sequentially. The propagation parameters obtained from the automatic method have been compared with the results of a previously implemented semi-automatic approach. Comparison between the two approaches revolves around the error involved, time complexity, and dependency on the morphology of the plasma structures. The results suggest that the proposed method can be adopted over the semi-automatic approach as it has less error, minimal dependency on the morphology of the structures, and less time-exhaustive. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Neural-network-based adaptive control for space manipulator system with actuator faults: a fully actuated system approach
Abstract: In the presence of actuator potential faults, this paper investigates trajectory tracking control for a free-floating space manipulator system (FFSM) subject to nonlinear uncertainties. The study aims to achieve desired tracking performance directly while addressing the challenges posed by system uncertainties and actuator faults. To accomplish this objective, the proposed control strategy relies on the high-order fully actuated (HOFA) system approach, consisting of three main components: a basic part designed to eliminate known nonlinearities and emphasize linear dominant terms; a neural network (NN)-based adaptation technique introduced to estimate the unknown bounds of actuators’ restricted effectiveness loss and lumped uncertainties; and a robustness component incorporated to mitigate the adverse effects of actuator bias faults. Utilizing Lyapunov stability theory, the NN-based adaptive fault-tolerant controller guarantees boundedness of all signals in the robust closed-loop system, while ensuring that position/velocity tracking errors are confined to a small neighborhood of zero relative to a well-designed eigenstructure. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is demonstrated through simulations conducted on a 6-DoF FFSM system. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Physical simulation method for meteoroid atmospheric entry with multiple-peaked light curves
Abstract: Meter-sized meteoroids typically exhibit asymmetric light curves with multiple peaks due to fragmentation and heterogeneous properties. This study proposes a systematic simulation method for modeling the trajectory, attitude, and structural evolution during their luminous atmospheric entry. The N-body meteoroid model incorporates irregular geometry, porous structure, and heterogeneous materials. In this approach, a cohesive contact model is employed to simulate the meteoroid's structural disintegration. Differential ablation and asymmetrical volume changes are applied to simulate the kinetic energy loss and reproduce the light curve. The equivalent cross-sectional diameters of the valid granules at the light curve peaks are calculated to quantify the expansion of fragments. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through its application to two meteoroid cases: the 2023 Beijing meteoroid and the asteroid 2024 BX1. The multiple light curve peaks observed for both meteoroids are successfully reproduced using the new approach. For large meteorites from 2024 BX1 with masses exceeding 100 g, the method predicts landing positions with an accuracy of approximately 1 km. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Ionosphere-thermosphere response to the January 14, 2022 moderate storm: ICON satellite observations
Abstract: We present a response of the ionized as well as neutral components of Earth's upper atmosphere to the 14th January 2022 moderate geomagnetic storm using ICON satellite observations. Global-scale analysis of ion density and thermospheric wind speed as a function of latitude and longitude covering 160–600 km altitude range provides descriptive illustrations of storm-time responses of different layers of the ionosphere. The storm induced disturbances at almost all altitudes considered in the study and the Hunga eruption caused high wind variations at lower altitudes (160–200 km). We also considered the effects of a co-incident Hunga Tonga volcanic eruption, while our focus remains on the ionosphere-thermosphere responses to the storm. Our analyses depicted strong equatorial and low latitude ion density enhancement on 14-01-2022 (12:01–23:59 LT) across almost all longitudes, which corresponds to the times after the sudden storm commencement (SSC). Compared to 13–14 January 2022 (00:00–12:00 LT), a high ion density is observed on 15-01-2022 (00:00–12:00 LT), especially over 0°-200° E longitudes. This ion density enhancement persists on 16-01-2022 (at all times of the day) with a similar scenario seen on 15-01-2022. Storm-enhanced wind speed irregularity decreases relatively with an increase in altitude. Ion density is higher in 12:01–23:59 LT than in 00:00–12:00 LT during all days considered. On 15-01-2022 (12:01–23:59 LT), fluctuating structure of ion density is observed in 100°–200°E longitudes over the dip equator region which was found to be associated with the Hunga eruption. Generally, the moderate geomagnetic storm caused a positive ionospheric storm, which enhanced ion density and triggered turbulence in the wind dynamics. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Importance analysis of geophysical effects for modeling of GNSS vertical time series
Abstract: Global navigation satellite system vertical time series have significant annual seasonal variations, which are partly generated by mass redistribution due to global cyclic migration of surface environmental loading. The Adaptive Boosting algorithm is used to reflect the importance of geophysical effects for modeling of GNSS vertical time series. To form the machine learning problem, temperature, atmospheric pressure, hydrological and polar coordinate data are considered as input data and GNSS vertical time series are considered as output data. In the modeling experiments, the Adaptive Boosting algorithm is introduced and evaluated using vertical time series collected from 28 GNSS reference stations. The results of the fitting experiments show that the average MAE value of the AdaBoost model is 3.91 mm. The results of the feature evaluation showed that the X pole had the highest average feature importance level of 22.95 and the temperature and atmospheric pressure data had the lowest level of about 19.20. Especially in the South and East Xinjiang, polar coordinate data have the highest level of relative feature importance in the vast majority of GNSS reference stations. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Dual-purpose use of the Santa Maria VGOS antenna for geodetic VLBI and methanol maser observations
Abstract: This paper presents the technical specifications and scientific capabilities of the Santa Maria VGOS antenna, a 13.2-meter radio telescope that is part of the RAEGE (Rede Atlântica de Estações Geodinâmicas e Espaciais) network in the Azores. While primarily designed for geodetic Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI), we demonstrate its potential for astronomical applications in single-dish mode, particularly for observing methanol masers at 6.68 GHz and 12.18 GHz. The technical description includes the broadband cryogenic receiver, backend system, and observing strategy, which enable high-sensitivity and high-resolution observations. We report the detection of methanol maser emission from sources including G009.621+0.196,G109.871+2.114,G111.542+0.777,G133.947+1.064, and G134.029+1.072, with flux densities comparable to or within the range of previous studies. By comparing these results with those from large interferometric arrays (e.g., VLA, EVN) and single-dish surveys (e.g., MMB, M2O), we highlight the single-dish VGOS antenna's suitability for long-term maser monitoring. We also discuss system limitations, such as sensitivity and spatial resolution, and propose mitigation strategies. These findings demonstrate the versatility of VGOS systems and provide a framework for leveraging a global VGOS network for cost-effective, flexible, dual-purpose geodetic and astrophysical research. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Simulation of the optical performance of a single corner cube retroreflector for the TianQin Project and lunar laser ranging stations
Abstract: The TianQin project is a space gravitational wave detection project initiated by Sun Yat-sen University. It has high requirements for detectors’ orbit accuracy in the stages of orbit entry and scientific experiment operation. Satellite laser ranging (SLR) is the space geodetic technique with the highest accuracy of range measurement, which is a commonly used method for satellite orbit determination. The corner cube retroreflector (CCR) works as the cooperative target of laser ranging. Since the Velocity Aberration (VA) effect for the specific orbit parameters of TianQin were never studied before, the CCR installed on the TianQin satellite cannot directly utilize existing CCR designs. This article mainly focuses on designing the dihedral angle offsets (DAO) for 80 mm-aperture solid/hollow CCR at wavelengths of 1064 nm and 532 nm, taking into account the laser polarization characteristics based on the VA effect. The simulation results indicate that the optimal DAO for the solid CCR are 0.3, −0.5, 0.3 arc-seconds and 0.3, −0.8, 0.3 arc-seconds, respectively, while for the hollow CCR, they are 0.6, −1.8, 1.1 arc-seconds and 0, −1.4, 1.5 arc-seconds. The number of echo photons is simulated based on the Tianqin laser ranging station parameters. For the TianQin satellite with an orbital altitude of 100,000 km, the number of echo photons from a solid CCR can reach 4.42 and 2.29 per second when using 1064 nm or 532 nm ranging, while the number of echo photons from a hollow CCR can reach 5.28 and 0.69 per second. The pulse broadening of a single CCR can be minimized to 42.66% of that of a CCR array with the same performance. The single CCR for TianQin reported in this paper is intented to be observed by ground station with lunar laser ranging capabilities. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: High-fidelity dynamics modeling of long-term station keeping around Earth-Moon synodic resonant halo orbits using solar sails
Abstract: Halo orbits in the Earth-Moon system are useful for many applications related to lunar exploration. Because they are generally unstable, station-keeping control is required for a spacecraft to prevent orbital escape. Solar sails are a propulsion system that produces thrust without consuming propellant. Although the magnitude of thrust is small, they are suitable for long-term station keeping around halo orbits. Because the direction of the Sun rotates in the Earth-Moon rotating frame, halo orbits around the Earth-Moon libration points must be synodic resonant to retain periodicity, where the ratio of the orbital periods to the synodic lunar period is rational. In this study, a long-term (e.g., more than 1 year) orbit design method in the high-fidelity ephemeris model was first developed. To make it possible, a successive orbit design method was devised, wherein relatively short-term orbits are sequentially designed such that they are connected to each other smoothly to retain the synodic resonance geometry. Simulation results indicated that it can be applied to at least around 2-year synodic resonant halo orbits. In addition, a station-keeping strategy to stay near the reference orbits under the influence of navigation error and attitude control error was developed. It was formulated using the state transition matrix and its Cauchy-Green tensor to minimize the future position and velocity error with respect to the reference orbit. The simulation results showed how the performance of the method changes according to the parameters (e.g., sail area-to-mass ratio, nominal Sun angle, and guidance and control frequency). © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: A 40-year record of the Earth's time-variable gravity field from SLR and DORIS
Abstract: Since 2002, the temporal variations of the Earth's gravity field are measured by the missions GRACE and GRACE Follow-On with unprecedented resolution and accuracy. In this study, we present a series of GRACE-like solutions going back to 1984 based on tracking data to 16 satellites, observed either by satellite laser ranging (SLR) or by means of the Doppler Orbitography and Radiopositioning Integrated by Satellites (DORIS) system. The match with GRACE in spatial resolution is achieved by representing the gravity field by empirical orthogonal functions (EOFs) obtained by a principal component analysis of the GRACE/GRACE-Follow-On solutions. To make the modelling more adaptive, the EOFs are supplemented by low-degree spherical harmonics. The presented time series is intended to replace a previous SLR-only solution applying the same parametrization. It is shown that the combined SLR/DORIS solution is clearly superior, reducing the average difference to the GRACE/GRACE-Follow-On fields by 10.6 percent; on a local scale, the error is reduced by up to 52 percent. As another enhancement, the beginning of the time series was advanced by eight years by extending the analysis to historical SLR data, albeit the noise in these early gravity solutions is higher, as expected. The time series now also includes a degree-1 solution based on an own inversion approach and using the surface mass distribution from the SLR/DORIS fields. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: A new science readiness level standard for space science investigations
Abstract: This article presents a new Science Readiness Level (SRL) Standard that has been developed at the Canadian Space Agency (CSA) for universal application to all space science investigations. Other authors have recognised that the traditional mission management process that relies on Technology Readiness Levels as the main tool to track mission maturity is missing important elements when it comes to science missions, and this is discussed. The motivation for developing a useable new science readiness assessment tool for missions of scale from CubeSats to flagships, in configurations as diverse as satellite constellations and ground-based instrument networks, with operations that can be robotic or crew-enabled, and with investigations that can range from traditional remote sensing to rover wet chemistry laboratories, is described. Universality of the derived SRL standard is achieved by assessing the quality and maturity of three independent elements of success that don't depend on the type of science, the project management structure, or the scale of the project: (1) the baseline investigation (2) the science success strategy, and (3) the science plan. Using language from NASA's Standard Principal Investigation-led Mission Announcement of Opportunity Template and in deliberate alignment with the European Space Agency (ESA) Earth Observation SRL scale, the final level of Science Readiness assesses Science Impact, underlining that the scale does not assess readiness simply to operate in the space environment, but readiness to deliver advances in knowledge associated with specific science objectives. Two examples are provided to illustrate the application of the Standard to investigations from different science disciplines and of widely different scope: a notional “FireSat” Cubesat mission, and a notional future “Mars life detection investigation at a methane seep”. It is expected that the CSA SRL Standard will evolve using lessons learned from users, and to align with evolving science practice and policy. The discussion addresses the international nature of science missions and science instrument contributions, suggesting value in convergence towards an international SRL standard. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Assessment of middle atmosphere climatology using lidar for aerospace applications
Abstract: This study evaluates temperature and density variations in the upper stratosphere and in the mesosphere using ERA-5 and NRLMSISE-2.0 models, by comparing them with our forty-years long temperature lidar observations. NRLMSISE-2.0, while reliable in terms of seasonal trends, is less accurate daily: it shows high biases with the lidar at high altitudes (globally less than 4 K below 50 km, up to 14 K at 80 km). The European Climate and Weather Forecast reanalysis model ERA-5 shows a bias to the lidar of −5 K the upper stratosphere but shows a larger difference reaching +20 K in the mesosphere. Lidar observations can reveal non-Gaussian distributions because of extreme events, such as Mesospheric Inversion Layers (MILs), minor and Major Sudden Stratospheric Warmings (m- and M-SSWs) or Double Stratopauses (DSs). These events are atmospheric particularities which should not be mixed with steady-state profiles to compute a mean climatology if the aim is to create a reference. To address this issue, a new methodology was developed to remove those events, resulting in what we called ”Steady-State” climatology. Our method based on lidar observation in four sites (Observatory of Haute-Provence, Reunion Island, Table Mountain and Mauna Loa) allowed us to give statistical information about these extreme phenomena. Furthermore, our findings show that when m-SSWs and MILs occur, the density profile deviates strongly from the NRLMISE-2.0 density, which highlights the need for refined atmospheric models for aerospace applications. Corresponding density differences between NRLMSISE and lidar can reach −15% and +25% at most for MILs and m-SSWs, respectively. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Optimal solar radiation pressure-assisted transfers from halo orbits to celestial bodies using genetic algorithm
Abstract: This study presents a solar sail trajectory design framework within the circular restricted three-body problem, focusing on transfers from halo and Lyapunov orbits around the sub-L<inf>1</inf> region to close-proximity passes of celestial bodies, particularly the Martian atmosphere in the Sun-Mars system and the Moon in the Sun-Earth system. Using a fixed-attitude, ballistic-like transfer strategy optimized via a genetic algorithm, the study achieves close-passes while minimizing both time-of-flight and sail cone angle. Numerical simulations show that Martian atmospheric passes are achievable with minimal control effort, requiring less than 14∘ cone angle and under 230 days across the halo orbit family. For the Moon case, close-passes are achieved with cone angles under 10∘ and transfer durations around 120 days across varying initial lunar positions from the chosen halo orbit. Simulation results confirm the method's robustness and consistency to changing initial conditions, with flexible tuning via optimization weights for the trade-off between flight time and cone angle. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Design of the TP-1B satellite's laser retro-reflector array and analysis of laser ranging
Abstract: To meet the highly precise orbit requirements of the Tianping-1B (TP-1B) satellite used for providing equipment calibration, a distributed laser retro-reflector array (LRA) has been designed with a weight of approximately 450 g, an effective reflective area of more than 4.6 cm2 and a field of view of more than 120° for performing laser ranging and supporting scientific test missions. The LRA consists of two types of cube corner retro-reflectors (CCRs) installed on the ground-facing side of the satellite: one is a nadir-facing CCR, and the other is six CCRs each featuring a 50° structural tilt angle. First, according to the orbital characteristics of the TP-1B satellite, its orbital flight duration has been predicted by the satellite laser ranging (SLR) station. Then, taking into account the spatial distribution of the CCR, the effective reflective area distribution of the LRA has been calculated. Furthermore, considering the additional phase shift caused by the dihedral angle offset of the CCR, as well as surface shape offsets in the reflective and incident planes, the far-field diffraction pattern of the CCRs has been plotted, Meanwhile, based on the laser ranging radar equation and the parameters of the SLR system, the number of laser echoes and laser ranging precision of the TP-1B satellite laser ranging have been calculated. Finally, SLR stations were used to track and perform ranging precision experiments on the TP-1B satellite. The actual measurement results at the SLR station show that the ranging precision is 5.3 mm and the average number of echo photons per second reaches 459. These results are consistent with the previous theoretical calculations and analysis, which further validates the effectiveness of the designed LRA and will guide the design of future LRA. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Spatiotemporal estimation and local driver analysis of fractional vegetation coverage in the Three-North region, China
Abstract: Understanding the spatio-temporal dynamics of fractional vegetation coverage (FVC) and its driving factors is imperative for advancing ecological management and fostering sustainable development. Towards the Three-North region of China, five distinct nonnegative matrix factorization models were employed to estimate FVC. The quadratic optimization derived from improved constrained nonnegative matrix factorization, IC-NMF<inf>2</inf>, was implemented to refine FVC estimation from 2000 to 2022. The spatial evolution pattern and change trend analysis were performed. The global and local drivers of FVC were analyzed using optimal parameter-based geographic detector (OPGD) and geographically weighted random forest (GWRF) model. The findings indicated that the IC-NMF<inf>2</inf> model outperformed other models in estimation accuracy and stability. FVC in the Three-North region had notable directional and regional characteristics, with a predominant tendency of either improvement or relative stability. However, localized degradation was observed, particularly in the Tianshan Mountains and the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region. Both OPGD and GWRF analyses consistently identified average relative humidity and accumulated precipitation as the primary global drivers of FVC, which showed a bi-enhance interactive effect. Average relative humidity was the first local influencing factor of FVC in most regions, showing strong spatial alignment with FVC distributions. By integrating local factor importance with trend analysis, more precise recommendations for ecological protection and management for sub-regions can be formulated. This study demonstrates great potential for application in other regions, especially in monitoring vegetation ecosystems and their dynamic responses to global climate changes in desert areas. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Autonomous correction of hydrogen maser clocks with a small X-ray pulsar detector in low earth orbit
Abstract: This study explores the application of autonomously correcting the offset of spaceborne clocks using a small X-ray pulsar detector in low Earth orbit. The XPNAV-1 observational data, which includes artificially introduced relative frequency deviations and drifts, is corrected using three methods: the residuals fitting method, the Significance Enhancement of Pulse-profile (SEP) method, and a newly developed technique called the Significance Fall of Pulse-profile (SFP) method. For a relative frequency deviation of k<inf>f</inf> = 1 × 10−11, the SEP and SFP methods require 315 days and 285 days of observation data to achieve corrections with under 5 % relative error, while the residuals fitting method necessitates 422 days of data. We also trace the UTC timestamps from XPNAV-1 back to two actual hydrogen clocks. The SFP method has the best correction accuracy and uses 12 and 15 months of observation data to achieve the clock offset of two clocks below 10 microseconds, respectively. To obtain valid results, at least 9 months of observation from XPNAV-1 is required to correct spaceborne cesium clocks, and at least 15 months of observation is needed for correcting spaceborne hydrogen clocks. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Spatiotemporal evolution of ecological environment and its industrial structure effect
Abstract: The eco-environmental issues arising from the industrial structure are directly related to the regional sustainable progress. The panel data of eco-environment and industrial structure of Shandong Province from 2003 to 2022 were used in this paper, the eco-environment quality was investigated by techniques like TOPSIS and principal component analysis. Additionally, the effects of industrial structure on eco-environment quality were examined through panel vector autoregressive model and its impulse response analysis and variance decomposition as well as a Granger causality test. The findings indicated that: (1) Between 2003 and 2022, the eco-environment quality of Shandong Province improved in all cities, with different levels of environmental pollution and governance, along with notable spatial and temporal disparities in eco-environment quality levels. The industrial structure of Shandong Province had gradually changed from a “two, three, one” pattern dominated by the secondary industry to a “three, two, one” pattern dominated by the tertiary sector, in addition the level of rationalization and advanced of the industrial structure had steadily increased. (2) A notable Granger causality existed among the proportion of output value of the secondary industry (PSI), the tertiary industry (PTI), the ratio of tertiary to secondary industry output (RTS), the diversity of the structure of the three industries (IS3), the advanced of the industrial structure (AIS), and the rationalization of the industrial structure (RIS, RISI), with eco-environment quality. Industrial structure change and advanced industrial structure had significant effects on eco-environment quality; industrial structure diversity had different effects on eco-environment quality in different periods; the industrial structure rationalization had negative effects on eco-environment quality. The impact of RIS and RISI negatively affected the level of eco-environment quality, which gradually weakened with the prolongation of time. Title: Importance of solenoid valve selection for performance of a cold gas thruster for an orbital experimental module
Abstract: Cold gas propulsion systems are the simplest manifestation of a propulsion system. This paper reports the design, development and testing of a gaseous helium based cold gas propulsion system for 1.0 N nominal vacuum thrust with a specific impulse of ∼200 s. The thruster is meant for 3-axis stabilization which calls for pulse mode operation with a high cyclic life and faster response. An in-house developed solenoid flow control valve (FCV) was used for on–off control of the thruster. The FCV is an important element present in the thruster due to the presence of movable parts. Hence, the propulsion system design is discussed with emphasis on the design aspects of the FCV for meeting the end use requirements. The important design aspects for the FCV are its ability to withstand a large cyclic actuation life requirement necessary for extended on-orbit operation, hard-on-soft sealing to ensure leak tightness at lower temperatures and its ability to respond in a faster manner for variations in operating pressure and supply voltage. In addition, its ability to withstand continuous coil energisation has also been demonstrated. The FCV is of flexure type construction with hinged ends resulting in an absence of sliding pairs. Hence, a cyclic life, demonstrated up to 1 million cycles, could be achieved for the FCV and the propulsion system. The valve along with the thruster has been extensively characterised and tested under vacuum condition for both steady state operation and pulse width modulation (PWM) with varying duty cycles. Correlation between sea level and vacuum thrust has also been established. It is seen that the vacuum thrust is more than the sea level thrust by 50 % under nominal operating conditions. Effect of nominal and off-nominal operating conditions on achieved thrust has also been studied. A detailed description of the valve design, thruster configuration, vacuum & sea level thrust observations, results of steady state and PWM testing, system on and off response are reported in this paper. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Assessment of Tianmu-1 multi-GNSS-R global soil moisture products
Abstract: Tianmu-1 (TM-1) is China's commercial remote sensing satellite constellation. Equipped with the global navigation satellite system occultation sounder M (GNOS-M), TM-1 generates soil moisture (SM) products based on GNSS reflectometry (GNSS-R) signals from the BeiDou navigation satellite system (BDS), global positioning system (GPS), Galileo, and GLONASS. This study comprehensively assessed the TM-1 global SM products authorized for use from October 1 to November 30, 2023. The assessment used two reference datasets: the soil moisture active passive (SMAP) satellite data and the international soil moisture network (ISMN) station data. The assessment of TM-1 Level 1 (L1) observations revealed stable instrument performance and strong agreement across multi-GNSS observations. The assessment of TM-1 Level 2 (L2) SM products revealed comparable performance among the systems. Comparison with SMAP SM data showed correlation coefficients (R) ranging from 0.85 to 0.86, root mean square error (RMSE) from 0.057 to 0.058 cm3/cm3, and mean bias error (MBE) from −0.008 to −0.005 cm3/cm3 for multi-GNSS observations. Comparisons with the ISMN 262 stations data showed R ranging from 0.60 to 0.66, RMSE from 0.060 to 0.064 cm3/cm3, and MBE from 0.002 to 0.011 cm3/cm3. Additionally, detailed analyses based on geographical zones and land cover classifications were conducted to refine the assessment results. The results confirmed that the TM-1 SM products have good accuracy and reliability, meeting the requirements for meteorological, hydrological, and agricultural applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Evaluating spectral indices from MODIS to predict maize and soybean regional yields
Abstract: A regression model with spectral information and dummy variables was developed and evaluated for predicting regional maize and soybean yield in the agricultural rain-fed region of Córdoba, Argentina. The study area comprises eleven departments that currently harvest more than 80 % of the provincial production of maize and soybean. In this study monthly Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) product (MOD13C2) and daytime Land Surface Temperature (LST) product (MOD11C3) derived from the MODIS sensor on board of TERRA satellite were used as model input. From these data Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI) was calculated and assessed also. In total, 19 summer crop seasons were analyzed between 2000/2001 and 2018/2019. There is a close and negative relationship between the NDVI, with both LST and TVDI. The best regression models with dummy variables were selected to estimate yield variation on a regional scale are integrated both with spectral information, as LST from January and NDVI from February, and factors linked to edaphic and management differences of each department, as well as the technological improvement in the model for soybean. By using an adaptation of the Leave One Out Cross-Validation (LOOCVad) technique, model accuracy was verified. The Residual Standard Error (RSE) obtained each year was, mostly, lower than that obtained for the entire record (general models). The mean RSE obtained for the set of years was 279.4 and 579.4 kg ha−1 for soybean and maize, respectively, which are below those obtained from the general models (354.7 and 788.6 kg ha−1, respectively). © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Reentry trajectory optimization with generalized waypoint constraint using adaptive matching-correction strategy
Abstract: The reentry trajectory optimization problem with the generalized waypoint constraint is solved using the adaptive matching-correction strategy in this paper. Generally, the reentry trajectory optimization problems are complicated due to their highly nonlinear dynamics and complex path constraints. Particularly, this paper considers the generalized waypoint constraint and proposes the adaptive matching-correction strategy to handle it. Two steps are included in the proposed strategy: “matching step” and “correction step”. The core idea is to find the edge that best matches the generalized waypoint constraint in the process of algorithm iteration, and then pull the edge into the constraint's zone. Compared with the traditional methods to cope with similar problems, the idea of multi-phase optimization is not needed, enhancing the algorithm's ability to tackle the abrupt appearance of the generalized waypoint. Extensive numerical simulations with comparisons are provided to demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed strategy. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Herbig AeBe stars with low infrared excess
Abstract: The spectral energy distribution (SED) curves analysis results for 48 Herbig AeBe stars (HAeBeS) and 13 young stellar objects from the Orion star-forming complex are presented. All 13 Orion stars and 8 HAeBe stars showed weak residual IR emission in the wavelength range λ ≥ 10 μm. Compared to other HAeBe stars, members of this subgroup show no or in some cases weak emission in the Hα line. We call this group “Weak Herbig AeBe stars” (WHAeBeS). The SED curves of the program stars are classified according to the magnitude of the IR excess radiation. The physical parameters of all the program stars were calculated. It was shown that the SED of the selected subgroup of WHAeBe stars and the stars of the Orion nebula OB1 are identical. Despite the youth of these stars, the reason for the relatively rapid dissipation of the circumstellar disk of the WHAeBe stars is unclear. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Comparative analysis of the seasonal and intra-seasonal geocenter motion derived from GNSS displacements: IGS Repro3 and Repro2
Abstract: Geocenter motion (GCM), driven by the largest-scale mass redistribution within the Earth system, requires precise determination for accurate geodetic measurements. This study investigates the contribution of recent International GNSS Service (IGS) data processing to GCM estimation by comparing results from two major reprocessing campaigns (repro2 and repro3) for the period 2003–2014. The degree-1 deformation approach is used in this study. We also examine the impact of two non-loading errors—draconitic errors (DRE) and thermal expansion of bedrock (TEB)—on these GCM estimates. At the annual timescale, repro3 GCM outperforms repro2 GCM in the Y component and shows a slight improvement in the X component, while both provide comparable estimates in the Z component. The relatively poorer performance of repro2 in the Y component is primarily due to more significant DRE, with the annual phase deviation reduced from 56° to 20° after DRE correction. TEB correction reduces the annual amplitudes of the Z component by approximately 1.7 mm, bringing them into better agreement with independent references. At the intra-seasonal timescale, repro2 exhibits more scatter compared to repro3, but DRE corrections improve their consistency. In conclusion, the more pronounced draconitic errors in repro2 contribute to its lower accuracy compared to repro3 for both seasonal and intra-seasonal GCM variations. With DRE mitigated, the consistency of repro2 GCM with independent references can be improved to a level comparable to that of repro3 in terms of overall agreement. We recommend mitigating DRE at the station position residual level for repro2. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Estimation of PM2.5 concentration in southern China using stacked machine learning models based on GNSS and radiosonde precipitable water vapor
Abstract: The technology for retrieving precipitable water vapor (PWV) using Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) has already reached maturity, and it shows a relatively strong correlation with PM<inf>2.5</inf>. Nevertheless, there is a lack of specifically developed algorithms for the relationship between PWV and PM<inf>2.5</inf>. This study focused on the southern region of China, data from GNSS stations, radiosonde (RS) stations, and co-located pollution monitoring stations in southern China during 2019–2022 were collected. The correlations between PM<inf>2.5</inf> and meteorological data, such as PWV, water vapor pressure, pressure, and temperature, were thoroughly investigated. It was found that the correlations between PWV and PM<inf>2.5</inf> were generally high yet exhibited regional variations. Based on these findings, a stacked machine learning (SML) model was innovatively developed for estimating PM<inf>2.5</inf> concentrations. During the model construction process, random forest (RF) and back-propagation neural network (BPNN) sub-models were developed, and the SML model was constructed by integrating the advantages of the two through the multiple linear regression model. The SML model performed outstandingly, its R2reached 0.88, and the root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) were significantly reduced compared with those of other models. It demonstrated a high-precision estimation ability in medium and low concentration intervals (0–10, 10–20, 20–30 µg/m3), with MAE and RMSE being respectively less than 4.50 µg/m3and 5.90 µg/m3. On an hourly scale, the SML model exhibited stable performance, with R2ranging from 0.84 to 0.93. In addition, the study also revealed that the PM<inf>2.5</inf> concentrations in southern China had significant regional characteristics, with the highest levels in the northeastern region and the lowest in the western region, which were closely related to terrain and population factors. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
