Title: Surface water salinity modeling for the Mekong Delta of Vietnam using hourly salinity observed data, remote sensing, and machine learning models
Abstract: Coastal and estuarine regions are facing the complicated problem of salinity intrusion. Remote sensing and Machine Learning (ML) have emerged as powerful tools for monitoring and predicting water quality changes. This study proposes a novel approach for surface water salinity prediction in the Mekong Delta, Vietnam, by integrating hourly in-situ salinity observation data, remote sensing data, and advanced ML models. We collected observed hourly data of 535 samples from 68 salinity stations in 2019 and 2020. Fifty-two influencing factors for salinity prediction modeling were prepared based on the critical review of previous studies, satellite images, and local geo-environmental conditions. The Bayesian Model Averaging technique is used to identify and select the optimal input variables for modelling. Three single and two ensemble ML models, including Bagging, Random Forest (RF), 1D-Convolution Neural Network (1D-CNN), Particle Swarm Optimization-Bagging, and Particle Swarm Optimization-Random Forest, were developed to create surface water salinity prediction maps. Based on the results of calculating popular statistical indicators, the Particle Swarm Optimization-Random Forest model has outstanding accuracy compared to the remaining ML models, so it is selected to generate the surface water salinity map for the study area. This map can assist decision makers in mitigating the impacts of saltwater intrusion on local livelihoods and planning for sustainable water resource protection. These contributions advance geospatial analysis for hydrological modeling and provide a robust framework for real-time salinity assessment in vulnerable coastal regions. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Machine learning-based modeling of tropospheric wet delay using layered atmospheric data
Abstract: Accurately modeling tropospheric delay remains a challenge due to the high spatiotemporal variability of water vapor in the lower atmosphere. In this study, Tropospheric Wet Delay (ZWD) was estimated using two machine learning (ML) approaches—Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM)—based on the ERA5 reanalysis dataset from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF). The models were trained on data from 2016 to 2020 and tested on 2021 data. Without incorporating surface meteorological data, XGBoost and LightGBM achieved root mean square (RMS) errors of 4.04 cm and 3.93 cm, respectively, both outperforming the GPT3 empirical model (4.20 cm). When surface meteorological variables were included, the accuracy improved further, with RMS values reduced to 3.17 cm and 3.06 cm. These results represent improvements of 26.96 % and 29.49 % over the traditional Saastamoinen model. Compared with the A&N(e<inf>s</inf>) model, improvements of 4.80 % and 8.10 % were achieved. Relative to the widely used Random Forest (RF) model, XGBoost and LightGBM reduced RMS errors by up to 19.14 % without meteorological data, and by 6.71 % when such data were included. Overall, both XGBoost and LightGBM demonstrate robust and consistent performance, maintaining high estimation accuracy under complex geographical conditions and varying climatic scenarios, outperforming both empirical and other ML-based models. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: First simultaneous Na/K lidar observations of meteor trains at São José dos Campos, Brazil (23.1°S, 45.9°W) using a dual-beam sodium and potassium lidar system
Abstract: We report the first simultaneous observation of meteor trains using the dual-beam sodium and potassium (Na/K) LIDAR system installed at São José dos Campos (23.1°S, 45.9°W), Brazil. We investigate the spatial and altitude distribution of meteor trains and evaluate their temporal variability throughout the year 2018. Through statistical analysis, this study provides critical insights into the physical properties and dynamics of meteor trains. The column abundance, density, Na/K ratio, duration, and frequency are systematically explored, shedding light on the dynamic characterization of these celestial phenomena. Our findings underscore that the majority of meteor trains detected by the lidar technique occurs within the altitude range of 83–90 km. These enhancements are more prominent in the K signal than the Na signal. In the analysis of the 2018 Na/K LIDAR data, it is evident that the majority of trains occur predominantly around 2100 LT, as seen in June and July, with the highest meteor activities being observed during April, May, July, September, November, and December. This temporal variability strongly suggests potential seasonal influences on the occurrence of meteor trains. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: PPP ambiguity resolution for GPS/Galileo/BDS-3 using different multi-frequency OSB products
Abstract: The implementation of observable-specific signal biases (OSBs) has significantly enhanced the efficiency of multi-frequency Precise Point Positioning (PPP) with Ambiguity Resolution (AR). By correcting raw observations for the corresponding code and carrier-phase biases, the integer properties of ambiguities can be restored for all frequencies or their combinations. Wuhan University and the French Centre National d’Études Spatiales (CNES) provide multi-frequency OSB products. The performance of these OSB products was evaluated using GNSS data from 50 IGS stations collected over a 30-day period in 2024 through the undifferenced and uncombined GPS/Galileo/BDS-3 PPP cascading AR method (PPP-CAR). The results demonstrate that, after applying the OSB corrections, over 87 % of the wide-lane (WL) ambiguity residuals for GPS, Galileo, and BDS-3 MEO satellites fall within ±0.15 cycles, with WL ambiguity fixing rates exceeding 95 %. For narrow-lane (NL) ambiguities, except for BDS-3 when using CNES-gbm products, more than 79 % of the residuals fall within ±0.15 cycles, with fixing rates surpassing 90 %. Substantial variations in ambiguity resolution performance and positioning accuracy were observed across stations, primarily linked to the receiver type. Septentrio receivers demonstrated superior performance compared to Trimble and Javad receivers. Incorporating multi-frequency observations significantly reduced PPP-CAR convergence times. Triple-frequency PPP-CAR achieved a 43 %–50 % improvement in convergence times compared to its dual-frequency counterpart. However, due to the inaccuracy of receiver PCO corrections for frequencies beyond the reference frequencies, the improvements of quad-frequency and five-frequency PPP-CAR over triple-frequency PPP-CAR were relatively limited. This limitation also led to slightly reduced vertical positioning precision for multi-frequency PPP compared to dual-frequency PPP after convergence. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Reclaimed-land subsidence mechanism analysis and evolution prediction of Tianjin Binhai New Area, China based on time-series InSAR observations
Abstract: Over the past few decades, as the scale of land reclamation projects has increased worldwide, monitoring and predicting the consolidation settlement of fill soil in coastal areas has become an important research topic in engineering construction and disaster prevention and mitigation. In order to thoroughly investigate the subsidence mechanism and deformation evolution of reclaimed land areas, a combined approach of temporal InSAR land subsidence extraction algorithm and ground deformation prediction model was attempted to develop a method for monitoring deformation and predicting consolidation in land reclamation areas. The Tianjin Binhai New Area (TBNA) was selected as a typical study area. Initially, 155 Sentinel-1A images from January 2018 to November 2023 were acquired, and the surface subsidence over the past five years in the region was monitored using an improved SBAS-InSAR algorithm model. Subsequently, by analyzing the effects of reclamation time, building loads, and groundwater extraction on surface subsidence, the surface subsidence mechanism in TBNA was revealed. Based on this, short-term and long-term deformation prediction models for consolidation settlement analysis of fill soil were constructed using LSTM model and geotechnical model, respectively. Finally, the spatial–temporal distribution and evolution prediction of uneven subsidence in TBNA were obtained. The results showed that the consolidation settlement of fill soil caused by land reclamation and excessive groundwater extraction are the main reasons for surface subsidence in TBNA. Currently, most of the reclaimed land areas in TBNA have entered the secondary consolidation and creep consolidation stages, with some coastal areas still in the initial consolidation stage, exhibiting higher subsidence rates. Serious subsidence is observed in the eastern coastal areas of TBNA, as well as in the northern areas of Hangu Street, Zaishang Street, and the southern towns of Xiaowangzhuang and Taiping, with a maximum subsidence rate of −237 mm/year. Combining LSTM model and geotechnical model for subsidence prediction facilitates complementary advantages, thereby enhancing understanding and anticipation of future subsidence trends in TBNA. The technical approach and research findings proposed in this study can serve as references for surface subsidence monitoring and safety risk assessment in TBNA and similar land reclamation areas. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Fibers drawn out from melting lunar regolith simulant: An appealing approach to support the lunar in-situ resource utilization
Abstract: Lunar regolith fibers fabricated in situ have the great potential to serve as engineering materials essential for various future lunar surface development missions. This study investigated the potential in-situ resource utilization of applicable fabrication equipment, the lunar regolith simulant fibers fabrication process, and the impact of thermal post-treatment on fiber properties. Initially, the thermokinetic and rheological characteristics of the HIT-L-1 lunar regolith simulant were analyzed. Subsequently, the influence of process parameters on fiber diameter and temperature was examined via numerical analysis and fiber fabrication experiments. Finally, the effects of thermal post-treatment on the microstructure, apparent state, and mechanical and surface properties of the fibers were evaluated. The results indicated that a simplified fiber preparation process tailored to the lunar surface environment could produce continuous lunar soil fibers successfully. Melt flow rate, winding speed, and traction distance were identified as the main process parameters affecting fiber diameter and temperature. The thermal treatment at 875 °C for 15 min resulted in a maximum tensile strength of 301.57 MPa for the lunar regolith simulant fibers, representing a 136 % increase. Thermal post-treatment is an effective way of adjusting the surface energy characteristics of lunar regolith simulant fibers. This paper provides a fundamental basis for lunar regolith production and broadens the path of in-situ resource utilization. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Enhancing Whipple shield defense against hypervelocity impacts: Influence of impactor geometry and surface treatments
Abstract: Spacecraft shields are essential for protecting spacecraft from damage caused by space debris and micrometeoroids. Depending on the source, naturally occurring impactors can reach velocities up to 72 km/s or even higher, particularly for stellar particles, presenting significant challenges for shield impact resistance. In order to enhance the debris protection performance of the Whipple shield, optimize debris cloud distribution, and improve debris kinetic energy dissipation, an SPH model incorporating eight non-spherical impactors and a Whipple shield was established and experimentally validated. This study investigates how the shape and state of the impactor, as well as the shield's surface condition, affect the impact process using LS-DYNA. Additionally, four reinforcement designs for the Whipple shield were numerically simulated and analyzed. Results indicate that a vertical impact from a dumbbell-shaped projectile causes the most damage to the shield. The tungsten carbide coating significantly improves the kinetic energy dissipation rate of the impactor, reaching 65 %, which is 137 % higher than that of the traditional Whipple shield. The shot-peened shield expands the fragment cloud distribution area, effectively blocking impact fragments. Statistical analysis of fragment shape and orientation reveals a significant linear correlation between the center of mass height, the shield's normal projected area, and the kinetic energy dissipation of non-spherical impactors. This model can predict Whipple shield damage from such impactors. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Destabilization mechanisms of electrostatic solitary waves in ion-acoustic regimes within collisionless cometary plasma
Abstract: This study investigates the dynamics of instability and energy of ion-acoustic waves (IAWs) in a magnetized, five-component cometary plasma comprising inertial hydrogen ions (H+), positively/negatively nonextensive charged oxygen ions (O±), and superthermal-distributed solar/cometary electrons. The work results in deriving the Zakharov-Kuznetsov (ZK) equation under nonextensive ion effects, showing how wave stability and energy transmission are governed by electron superthermality, ion nonextensivity, and magnetic geometry. The findings show that phase velocity increases with solar electron densities and superthermality, but decreases with ion nonextensivity of oxygen ions, emphasizing the competition between the ion-driven dissipation and electron thermal pressure. Increased Landau damping and increased electron pressure cause lower negative oxygen ion density to amplify the instability growth rate, gr, by upsetting charge neutrality and causing ion drifts; higher electron densities, on the other hand, cause gr to increase. Energy, E<inf>n</inf>, accumulates with solar electron density, oblique propagation, θ, and weaker magnetic fields, ω, via enhanced nonlinear steepening and dispersive broadening. In contrast, gr peaks at parallel propagation (θ→0°) but declines at oblique angles (θ>θ<inf>c</inf>) as a result of magnetic stabilization. Notably, magnetic fields suppress gr at high θ while enhancing E<inf>n</inf> through wave broadening. The study identifies a critical distinction: E<inf>n</inf> depends on nonlinearity-dispersion balance, whereas gr hinges on electron–ion coupling and resonant interactions. By connecting microscopic wave activity to macroscopic instability thresholds, these findings provide cometary plasma models forward and help to understand Rosetta mission data and forecast wave-driven heating in cometary environments. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Understanding the IBEX ribbon using the kinetic model of pickup proton transport in a scatter-free limit
Abstract: One of the most remarkable discoveries by the Interstellar Boundary Explorer (IBEX) is the ribbon – a narrow band of enhanced energetic neutral atom (ENA) fluxes observed in the sky. The prevailing explanation attributes the IBEX ribbon to the secondary ENA mechanism. In this process, “primary” hydrogen ENAs, produced via charge exchange between solar wind protons and interstellar hydrogen atoms within the heliosphere, travel beyond the heliopause and undergo further charge exchange with protons of the local interstellar medium (LISM), generating pickup protons. Some of these pickup protons subsequently experience charge exchange with interstellar hydrogen atoms, forming “secondary” ENAs, some of which travel back toward the Sun and are detected by the IBEX. This paper presents a kinetic model developed to simulate secondary ENA fluxes. Ribbon simulations are performed using global distributions of plasma and hydrogen atoms in the heliosphere derived from a kinetic-magnetohydrodynamic model of the solar wind interaction with the LISM. The model accounts for all relevant primary ENA populations, including neutralized thermal solar wind protons, neutralized pickup protons, and ENAs originating in the inner heliosheath. The transport of pickup protons beyond the heliopause is described by the focused transport equation for a gyrotropic velocity distribution in the scatter-free limit, assuming no pitch-angle scattering or energy diffusion. Our simulations qualitatively reproduce IBEX-Hi (0.5–6 keV) ribbon observations and exhibit good quantitative agreement at low heliolatitudes. However, the model underestimates fluxes at high heliolatitudes, likely due to the omission of non-stationary solar wind behavior in the stationary framework used in this work. The study highlights the importance of ENAs from the inner heliosheath, a population considered for the ribbon production in the frame of the kinetic model of pickup proton transport in the heliosphere for the first time, for accurately reproducing ribbon fluxes observed by IBEX-Hi at the highest energy steps. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Multipath mitigation for IGS GNSS stations and its application in GNSS satellite clock offset estimation
Abstract: Multipath errors, significantly influenced by the observing environment, persist as a critical factor impeding the performance of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) applications. Numerous studies have focused on multipath error modeling and corrections for specific sites. However, the impact of multipath errors still requires to be sufficiently evaluated for International GNSS Services (IGS) stations and considered in the satellite clock offset estimation process. In this study, congruent grid based multipath hemisphere model at the resolution of 1° in elevation angle and azimuth are established for 105 globally distributed IGS stations. The contributions of multipath correction are evaluated by daily static Precise Point Positioning (PPP) at those IGS stations, as well as satellite clock offset estimation using those IGS GNSS observations. Analysis results suggest that obvious multipath errors exist for those IGS GNSS observations and have to be accurately corrected. After multipath correction, the RMS of line-of-sight pseudorange/phase observation residuals declined by 41 %/10 %, 25 %/5 %, and 42 %/16 % for GPS, Galileo, and BDS, respectively, while the daily static PPP accuracies improve by 77.26 % for the up component on average. With respect to satellite clock offset estimation, the average STDs drop by 15.74 %, 11.84 %, 7.74 %, and 8.63 % for GPS, Galileo, BDS IGSO, and BDS MEO satellites. All these results prove the necessity of multipath correction for IGS stations in their applications to satellite clock offset estimation, and possibly satellite precise orbit determination, or other geophysical researches in the future. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
